Sr. A. Maria Eletta Convertini

MADRE ROSA, A MOTHER

English translation of Rosa Gattorno una madre (Rome 1987)

Preface by Fr. Valentino G. Macca di S. Maria, OCD

M. Rosa, which richness of the spirit and in humanity!

Humble and devoted enwrapped in a mystery of simplicity and nobility, always looking at God, her Love, and with the gaze attentive to all people especially the humble and those most forgotten. She is a mystic woman and at the same time of a great tirelessly activity, with two eyes that were penetrating deeply the soul of those who were meeting her. It would have been enough to encounter her once in order to keep her memory as a continual presence; a presence that, through her, one was feeling drawn near to God. It was making feel good and serene, it was making peace with own life attracted to love it more even in time of cross and suffering; it was a challenge to pray more and to smile, it was as opening more the heart and the pocket towards the poor, the last, attracting others to become like her: a gift of gentle charity attentive and effective for whoever was in need of a smile, of a word of encouragement and of help. Most of all was a kind of experiencing what God had communicated to her with so much force and abundance when had moulded her with a spirit so rich and sensible of a Mother. All those who in a special way could experience her intimacy, and not only her Daughters, were having a sensation to find in her a wonderful and visible reflex of the tenderness of God who is for each one of us more than a Mother as St Teresa of Lisieux, based on Scriptures was saying.

It was the joyful experience in the contemporary witnesses, who were telling it with emotion. An ever living and sweet memory of her maternal face when she was in prayer and when she was at the service of the poor; when she was opening herself to that communion so supernatural and so human that in God one could sense her, more then a sister, as Mother who is ready to mysteriously give life. Was He not calling her to be Mother now and forever?

It is to welcome a study of her personality that reveals this maternal aspect of Rosa Gattorno. It is a gift that helps to penetrate, praying and contemplating that special maternal gift that is Rosa.

In his Providence God planned that at the age of twenty two Rosa could marry Gerolamo Custo, becoming mother of three children: Carlotta, Alessandro and Francesco. It was a painful maternity even though in the joy of the gift of self for the economical situation of the breakout of Gerolamo, and soon after his sickness and death still young in March 1858. Rosa does not close in herself: it is contrary to her nature. Alone, with worries and anxieties, she is ever more open to the Charism of Maternity to her children and to the poor widening the richness of her heart and her love. More than before she is a Mother and only a Mother! One could say that God is at game with this young lady of Genova who attracts her in the centre of his graces, making deeper her maternity and giving to it a new face of chastity which she bound herself with a Vow after the death of her husband, adding soon after, the Vow of Poverty, an interior richness for a greater donation to which LOVE was preparing her.

It is in this prospective that in the city of Genova first, she starts experiencing a life oriented to the Religious Consecration: maternal initiative that is named first on the Immaculate and after on St. Anne, in Piacenza and Roma in Via Merulana where the mother will spend her last years to be open to the light of the Redeemer in May 1990, when sister death would come to carry her soul in the bosom of He from whom every Fatherhood takes its name and every maternity, as Pope John Paul I reminded in one of his catechesis.

Her programme? To be a Mother.

Her name? A mother and only a Mother

Her style? Maternity that is offered.

Her pedagogy? As a Mother caring, loving and serving.

The same way she wanted to be a Mother, she was expecting her Daughters to be “Little Mothers”, those called in places of responsibilities of direction, formation and guide of the Sisters. All this in the name of Mary and of the Holy Mother St Anne, that the prophetic intuition of Fr Bernardo M. Clausi of the Minimum had indicated as Title of the Family of M. Rosa.

The correspondence confirms the dates of the Beatification and offers thousands of details on the spirit of maternal formation of Rosa Gattorno. She was a woman of balanced personality who without sentimentalism was looking for strong women. She was educating them with the grace that goes moulding, in sacrifices, in work, in the renouncing of self and the total self giving. She was looking in each and every Daughter of St Anne a Mother like her, on the example of Anne, of Mary totally oriented to the gift of life, to God, in the Community and to brothers/sisters.

The publication of the correspondence of Mother Rosa reveals treasure of tenderness, sweetness, her inner strength, woman of the gentle and noble intuition, of attentive respect for the different character and gift of nature and grace, of firm service to the project of God in each person. But all the Letters that are thousands and thousands reveal the Gift that God made to the Church in Rosa Gattorno creating in her a heart so close to his own, totally committed in oblation, in a life joyfully determined in the offering, nurturing and perfecting life in others.

The present study analyzes with sobriety and competence the gift of maternity of Madre Rosa Gattorno. It is not around pious consideration or just literally whims. It is a serious research, based on secure sources on what can help to understand the Mother of the Daughters of St Anne, in the itinerary on which God guided her in her first natural family blossomed from the sacrament that made of her, spouse and mother at natural and spiritual level, then in the Institute in which God wanted to be expressed in the fullness, if we can dare to say so.

The mystery of a maternity that is simple and complex, proved and blessed, with obstacles and rewarded above any expectation. It’s not without surprise that in 1900 when Rosa ends her earthly pilgrimage, it is known that her maternity is expanded also beyond Oceans. Almost 4000 Religious were calling her Mother and they experienced it even though far away physically from her in the 368 Communities in Italy, America, Africa; Families where love reigns and each one grow in the gift of love, under the secure guide and closeness of the heart of Mother Rosa.

In these last years the work for the conclusion of the Cause of Beatification has re-started. The study of the Processes of the Writings of the Mother, the large precious Documentation call for praising God for what has accomplished in her humble Servant. In all this gift of the Lord, in all her generous answer to the Spirit of Jesus, one thing is evident: in Rosa the Father invites to contemplate his love and his mercy, his bounty and his patience, his generosity the way was welcomed and brought to perfection in the experience of the humble woman called to be at the beginning of a religious experience of Consecration under the Name of the Mother of the Immaculate, St Anne; a woman that will for ever be a Mother. In the moment when Vatican II has called us back to the contemplation of the Church, that in Mary and with Mary, is Mother; Is it not a spring of ecclesial hope the knowledge, the imitation, the invocation of Mother Rosa Gattorno?

To this is oriented the present work of Sr. A. Maria Eletta Convertini, the first that invites to many other investigations and researches that place in the spirit the desire to know ever more this Mother that God gave to the Institute of the Daughters of St Anne to the whole Church. To find a Mother it is to find the source of LIFE. That life which in Mother Rosa Gattorno was God, loved and served up to the complete sacrifice for the joy of the children of God.

Valentino G. Macca di S.Maria, OCD

Relatore della Causa di M.Rosa

Rome, March 25th 1987

Feast of the Annunciation of the Lord

Who is Rosa Gattorno? She is a woman who is wonderfully rich in “Gifts of nature and grace”. God has entrusted her with a “special” mission of motherhood: to be at the service of life, in every condition, and in a universal dimension, in the historical realities of her time. She expresses her generous and faithful answer by offering her whole life to God, in a relationship of mystical offering and in apostolic action.

A “sign” of irrefutable evidence of apostolic action is the development of the many communities of the Religious “Family”, established by Mother Rosa in northern and even more successfully, in southern Italy, between 1866 and 1900. These were very “difficult” years for the kingdom of Italy, that had very recently been officially proclaimed, and that had not yet overcome the difficult process of unification, and problems connected with it. Another sign of her apostolic action was the development of communities in South America and in Africa, in even more “difficult” circumstances. Another important sign was the fact that many young ladies joined the Daughters of St. Ann, attracted by the charm of her charism and calling her “mother”.

These spiritual Daughters have communicated an accurate portrait to the future generations, by “narrating” and bearing witness to her life, by developing a veneration to her person, and practicing in concrete daily events that have historically preserved her memory, starting from the collection of her writings, the publication of a first biography in 1937, of a second one in 1969, together with other studies on her personality. The second biography was published for the purpose of providing information to everyone. Mother Rosa is a person who is still relevant to today’s world. The number of lay persons, who are inspired by her witness as a strong, brave lady, is increasing. They know that she belonged completely to God. Her motherhood is a gift that has been welcomed not only by the Daughters of St. Anne, but also by an increasing number of spiritual children. This is a sign of our time, one that causes us to become attentive. Mother Rosa wishes to re-express her mission of motherhood in today’s world that is just as difficult and filled with problems as it was in her time. How can this be done?

This is a question that is asked by many. Many persons wish to know more information about the life and work of Mother Rosa Gattorno. Many try to listen to her voice that almost “speaks” in her written works. The purpose of this study is to provide an answer, to the question of establishing an historical “dialogue” with the Mother, and to greater and deeper things that are emerging. This is an answer based on examining the original “sources” that consist precisely of the very numerous Letters written by the Mother, the Letters written by the Custo’s children, and by the Daughters of St. Anne and to a limited extent of the Memoirs.

This study attempts to understand Mother Rosa in the perspective of motherhood, as a direct and personal agent in the interpersonal relationships, with her own children, and with her spiritual children. This study attempts to describe the richness of her maternal attitude open to God and people that is disclosed to every one in the “climate’ of feelings and attitudes. It attempts to consider her actions inspired by the attitude of motherhood. This is the connecting link in the research. The objective is exclusively focused on her, who writes and speaks, and who speaks to us through her writings. The quotations are therefore, numerous. We regret that many quotations have been deliberately omitted, for understandable editorial reasons, because the use of many quotations would have been repetitive. The whole materials used in the development of this work, is therefore based not only on quotations mentioned in this study, but also by other similar that are not mentioned.

The sources, almost all of them not yet published, confer authority to the present study. Nonetheless, this study is only a limited approach to the correspondence, and is only a limited contribution to the knowledge of Mother Rosa.

It is a very limited answer to the important questions that concern the life and work of Mother Rosa Gattorno, and it is a filial recognition of gratitude towards Mother Rosa, for her valuable service to the church, for her wonderful service for the cause of the kingdom of God that Mother Rosa served faithfully, by giving “everything and also her own life”.

MOTHERHOOD:

THE HEART OF ROSA GATTORNO’S CHARISM

Awareness of the gift.

Motherhood is the heart of Rosa Gattorno’s vocational charism. Her person was emanating the maternal feelings flowing from her soul. And she was also aware of being a messenger with the mission of conveying God’s love to others. Therefore she gave her “gift of motherhood without limits, and without reward.”1

Mother Rosa was as constantly dedicated in forming the Daughters of St Anne, in the spirit of the family of the Holy Mother of Mary Immaculate.

She recommended Sr. Francesca Camisa, the superior of the community of Sampierdarena:

“Your poor mother can only pray to the Lord every day, so that he may help his Daughter to become holy, and may give her the necessary good understanding for the management of her community: Prudence, Meekness and charity; with these three virtues, that I hope God the Father will grant you, you will be able to guide the Daughters of St Anne on the way of perfection.”2

And to Sr.Adelaide Pezzoni:

“… charity, kindness; the kindness of the words of the mother who correct her daughters, ensure that the heart of a Sister may not avoid making necessary changes, and become a true Daughter of St. Anne.”3

Pervaded by a maternal love, she treated the nuns with kindness and understanding. To Sr. Veneranda Pico, who complained about her silence, she wrote in 19th May, 1879:

“My dear daughter … Banish all sad thoughts, and consider that your mother thinks of you every day, and (if one may say this), you are her favourite nun! Oh, my dear child, when will you be persuaded to believe in the love that I bear for you? Farewell, I am yours for eternity.”

Her letters to her daughters contain and express, with an emphasis of unmistakable intensity, the treasure of tenderness and dedication of her motherhood fully experienced -she was a mother in the flesh- “ by the will of man” (John, 1,13) and she was a mother in the Spirit too. She used to start her letters with expressions of tender love:

“My dear daughter, my beloved daughter, my ever loving daughter, and other similar expressions, and conclude her letters with endings such as: “Your poor mother”; ‘your poor mother but nonetheless, your mother believe me, I am your poor mother Rosa, now and for all eternity.”

It was dear to her that all the Daughters should address her by using one name: Mother. When Sr. Francesca Camisa, one of the first nuns thought that would be appropriate to use the title of “Foundress”, in a letter to Mother Rosa, her reply even though her language remained calm and affectionate expressed unusually severity:

”My Francesca, my dear daughter, first of all: unless you wish me sending back all your letters, change the method of addressing me. Here is the address you must use: “ to Sr. Anne Rosa Gattorno” If you write anything else, I will send your letter back, and I will no longer write to you, because, my dear, I have enough problems that afflicts me, and for me these words are repugnant, they are words that announce a purely infernal way of life. I was never important, and I am not important now; by your good will, you all call me with the name of mother, even though I do not deserve it.”4

She learned how to be a mother by raising her children: Carlotta, Alessandro, and Francesco. She nurtured them for nine months she saw their births, and their growth.

She took care of them, so that their lives would be beautiful and wholesome.

The same she did with her spiritual Daughters, and could not do differently. She explained this in a letter that referred to two nuns, whom she had welcomed as orphans in her community, many years before she wrote the letter, who had both become Daughters of St Anne:

”I always remain their poor mother, who loves them in the heart of St. Anne Mother of the Immaculate Virgin, and everyday prays for them, and then says: Mother, look at these children, who were raised with divine providence, and see them now, they have become nuns, they have learned well their lessons in faith, they have become true brides of Christ. It is a great comfort to know that now I have many spiritual adopted Daughters, who will share the joy of a happy eternal life with me!”5

A mother, even though her children grow and become mature and autonomous, maintains and strengthens the links of love with them. It is a law of motherly love, and Mother Rosa as all mothers, obeyed this law. She wrote to Sr. Giuseppa Troni, who lived in La Paz, Bolivia on 25th May 1879:

”…It is now twenty days since I do not receive any letters, and I say: What is my Daughter doing? Does she perhaps believe that I do not feel the void left behind by her absence? Dear Daughters! The nuns who are in Italy do not concern me so much as the nuns who are in foreign countries. I ask you to write more often, and I pray often for you. I ask: what will they do? They have left with me their hearts and their wills. I remain always faithful, and everyday I offer them to God, and I pray that the Crucified may keep you always in Him. Oh! Sweet dwelling place where peace love and joy reign! You, who wish to be happy, be faithful to Him, and you will find in Him Joy and love and every sweetness, I hope that you will give me many news about your good works. I have a great desire to hear them from you. Dear Daughters think of your poor Mother: It’s true that I am ugly and old, but I repeat, I am also your Mother! Even the poor children, if they have a poor and ugly mother, they still love her because she is their mother, and they prefer her to princes, and to the nobility of the world. Enough of this, I wish to banish from my mind the thought, the terrible thought that torments me so much, that you may have forgotten, or that your hearts may have grown cold.!! No, no, I know that these are sad thoughts, and I want to banish them!” 6

Apart from the strength and emphasis of her style (that is nearly a hammering style, in the emphasis given by the imperatives, such as “think”, and “I am”, which is repeated, note also “but yet I am”) This last sentences seem to express in a synthetic way, the clear awareness of motherhood felt by Mother Rosa. In her life, motherhood is a reality experienced at first: her motherhood in the flesh, by means of the will of man, later: motherhood through the Holy Spirit.

These words express the reality from the first stage of motherhood, from which its development derive having the gifts of grace intertwined with the human, without diminishing its peculiarity, they perfect and strengthen gifts and qualities of the person.

The two levels of maturity enlighten one another, and become integrated. The “poor” and “old” recall the pleasant reality of married life, in the joyful love of the family. But “poor” and “ugly”, is the language of a humble person, who recognizes herself as such, by no longer referring to a worldly value, but rather referring to the Wealth and Beauty of All, of her Good “the Being of her life “, and the sole reason of her life.

Mother Rosa herself completed her thoughts by saying: “But the poor children love their mother, prefer her to princes and to all the nobility of the earth.” this is because children have a pure heart and a clear vision of life, without hypocrisy or lies. Rosa’s Gattorno’s motherhood then, develops on the two levels human and spiritual, in two stages of life towards fullness.

Being aware of having such a gift, she will speak to her Daughters always, and only, as mother. She will tell them, towards the end of her life:

“…I love you, my Daughters, but in God’s love, in the immense love that remains in all hearts.”7

In the depth of the gift

Rosa’s vocation is obviously, inserted in the great wonderful plan of salvation of the Father. Like any other creature, she is freely called, by God’s grace, in the intimacy of her heart, in a dialogue of communion with God, in the mystery of the divine “You” by means of a strong and indefinable love; a divine enticement that matches the deepest aspirations of every human being.8

Rosa was sensitive about the transcendence. The faith in God, that she had known as a young girl in her family, by her mother’s good example and teaching, become stronger and developed during her life. Rosa’s faith became a relationship of devotion and obedience, an orientation towards the values of honesty, integrity and goodness, seeking and practising the fulfilment of that goodness planned by God for her.

2.1 Vocation orientation

Rosa Gattorno did not leave any written records that deal with the first period of her life, which could have provided useful information for us. Therefore, we cannot penetrate the intimacy of her soul, where a reciprocal convergence of communion, in the dynamism of demand and consensus until Rosa made her radical decision to obey God’s will. One cannot define the development or the duration of this period. Of certain events during her childhood and adolescence, from her habitual behaviour in her relationships with her family and with others, from various conversations, one may only see some reflections of her inner world, of the feelings in her heart.9

At the age of eleven, she received her First Communion and the Sacrament of Confirmation. Rosa perceived the Eucharistic experience, the gift of the Holy Spirit, as something wonderful, astonishing and joyful. As a mysterious fascination of enlightenment that opened her conscience to the Truth. Her mother became aware of these feelings and kept them in her heart rejoicing for her beloved daughter.10

Rosa from this time onwards oriented herself towards the Christian values of faith, of prayer, of Love. She prays and teaches others to pray, she learns catechism, and she teaches the catechism to her younger brothers. She is sensitive to the needs of those who live near to her she helps others foreseeing their needs. She “sees” the poor, and helps them. With tact, kindness, love, grace and the enthusiasm of a “properly raised” girl, she is prepared to become a good, and reliable, mother of children, Her life as an adolescent was spent without any shocks, because her parents favoured the development of her identity, orienting her in choosing existential values, that could help her both for her own formation and her relationships with her friends and her peer group. Her first orientation of prayer and faith influenced her towards practicing these values in everyday life, in guiding all her actions. Her choice to follow God’s values was challenged by some non-believers who visited her family. Her values were not weakened or altered by this experience. Instead of being weakened the experience of becoming familiar with the ideas and values of non-believers, strengthened her faith, a faith that was based on rationality11. At the end of her adolescence, her personal identity was clearly defined. “The challenges from God” and her answer to him were certainly converging.

2.2 The choice: Marriage

But the fundamental choice raised other questions: What was her role according to God’s plan in her life, in the society and in the church? What kind of life was she called to follow? The one as Consecrated Celibacy or Marriage? She felt a certain predisposition towards Religious Life. She consulted her feelings and her inner questions concerning her future with persons who could help her to clarify the consistency of her intentions; first of all her parents helped her to do this task. She pondered, she prayed, and allowed herself to be enlightened. She finally decided in favour of married life in obedience to God’s will that was shown by the mediators of his will. On 5th December 1852, she married Gerolamo Custo.

She left the home of her parents, and now she had her own home. She experienced the presence of God by the faithful love of her husband. She felt surrounded by the Father’s providence and goodness, which filled her life with happiness and joy. She experienced the development of peace, serenity and joy. She became mother three times: at the age of twenty five, her first born child was born: Carlotta (1853), followed by Alessandro (1855) and Francesco (1857).

2.3 ‘Motherhood’

The experience of motherhood, the mysterious contact with life at its sources, the unique relationship with others, who were sustained by her very nourishment, and entrusted to her as precious gift, to defend, take care of, to develop it and encourage its growth, offered to Rosa Gattorno, access to the immense warmth of life. The deep relationship established between Mother Rosa and her children are unforgettable. The woman’s inner world is humanity rich in “spirituality”, in emotions and in free and conscious sharing. A mother has with the human being living in her a relationship of love, acceptance, and affectionate attention. In this kind of relationship is based the specific human aspect of Motherhood. In it a very complex dimension, which establishes links between a mother and her child and reaches the root of subconscious becoming conscious, they are sublimate and are for ever.

These links become conscious, become spiritual, they acquire values they become permanent links.12 The period of development, of an intimate, symbiotic relationship between mother and child, is the foundation of motherhood. For nine months a vital process of symbiosis occurs, when the mother seems to be a prisoner of her own perfection, and life may not emerge from her, without wounds or changes.13

But even after a child begins his/her own life after birth, the mother will continue to take care of her child, in a new kind of relationship, a spiritual relationship, that is just as important as the biological one.

To take care of a child, to give him love, to provide security and stability, to raise a child, to participate in a child’s destiny, is the normal dimension of all human motherhood. To understand the mother’s life experience, to understand the feelings of love, to utilize one’s own ability to be recognized by others for one’s own merits, to assert one’s own rights, until a child becomes autonomous adult, is the essence of a filial relationship. Therefore every mother, if she really wishes to be a mother, must listen carefully, one may say, to the teaching of her young child, that the child may learn the difficult process of becoming a mature adult.

This is why motherhood is a process that continues for the whole life, and is prolonged with the gift of spiritual maternity, in the attempt to give one’s own spiritual life to the child, just as a body was given till reaching to the total, and sublime, gift of self to a child accepted as distinct from self.14

Downfall of the family-life

The experience of participating in the love of God that was expressed in the gift of life to her children, in the joy of the newly started family, was soon replaced by the opposite experience of sorrow and separation.

An early financial misfortune that was overcome with courage and sacrifice, was soon followed by Gerolamo’s illness, and by his death, on the 9th March 1858, he died at the age of thirty-one. Three months later, his young son Francesco died. This was a terrible down fall. Rosa was now devastated, almost inert, and without the will to live anymore. She was a widow at the age of twenty-seven she was financially poor, in the middle of quarrelling about money between her parents, and her parent’s in-law. Even her furniture was confiscated. She gratefully accepted her father’s offer, and returned to the Gattorno’s family home, to the house that she had left six years before the tragic events, when she had been greeted with joy by her husband, and she dreamed of the happiness in her family, of intimate and lasting love. With her faith, Rosa overcame her resentment against unjust behaviour of her parent in law, and she, who was the greatest victim of this conflict, made peace. She was building peace, for love of God, and also for the sake of her innocent children. Her children had a right to life, to joy, to happiness in a family life. With a “Supplementary’ amount of love she tried to fill the void left by their father’s death by providing a climate of security and balance and she also tried to harmonize the role played by the paternal grand parents and to develop normal family relationships.

The reunited family looked to the future with optimism and hope, sustained by the financial assistance provided by her “Dad” Francesco and by Rosa’s spiritual richness. With her attitude of calm, rationality and happiness, she developed a positive climate and a positive family life, a family life that was friendly, loving, and new and she developed relationships based on love, acceptance, trust and mutual love. Rosa had become the heart of hope for her children and for her own parents they experienced her as part of their life and source of help for their own future.

3. On a broader horizon

Rosa who was affected by the harshness of the cross, tried to understand the significance of this experience. By spending a great deal of time in prayer, by contemplating Christ the Crucified, who is the only sinless Person, she could find sense of all her sufferings. And this understanding enlightened her. A new life began in her soul. Her motherhood developed from Sacramental love through human bonds, sought a new extension, with parameters that had no quantitative or a space limits. Christ’s command, “love one another, as I have loved you” developed in her soul a new ability of loving and encouraged her to dedicate her life to Christ and to her fellow human beings.

She served her fellow human beings by her apostolic action which was inspired by the Holy Spirit. The “method” developed from the heart of Christ, who invented a thousand formulas to express his tenderness and did good to everyone up to the point of dying on the Cross, was for Rosa a call to go beyond the limits of her own family and of her paternal home, to reach the broader horizon of the family of God, authentically represented by the local church and by her own Parish.

3.1 A new vocational call

In these contexts, Rosa discovers the open field of charity, and she explores this field where the cry of weakness and poverty is stronger:

“…. Being free from all ties, I dedicated myself to works of charity with greater zeal I visited sick persons in the hospitals, I visited ill persons in their homes, I assisted them as much as I could and I attended to all their needs. By the grace of the Lord I became aware that all my love was becoming weak, and nothing was more comforting than my God, who gave me great joy.15

The “Memoirs” are spiritual writings, and contain mostly autobiographical information. These words, that begin the Memoirs, are a great revelation. Since 1858, when her husband died Rosa is free to make a free choice: “I attended”, “I visited” and her attitude towards God and human affairs is completely different, “Nothing was more comforting than my God, who gave me great joy”, the language is clear and explicit. This is an experience of knowing God, and everything is not important when compared to this experience. A very severe regime of fasting and penance began; Rosa wished to make God the Centre of her whole life. She strengthened a relationship of trust and love with Mary the Mother of Jesus:

“I received great favours from the Most Holy Mary during the Novena of our Lady of the Vine, while the Holy Sacrament was exposed during the time of Benediction I saw on the Most Holy Host the Blood of Christ that seemed to be flowing from it. I cannot express my thoughts after seeing this vision I can only say that I felt consumed by a divine fire”.16

3.2 A bride of her Good Lord

Rosa was clearly aware of the total call made by God. She felt a deep sense of her unworthiness, as a void that must be filled: “It means nothing at all, to give our entire selves to him, when I compare this to God’s infinite greatness.”17 Rosa dedicates her whole life to God, through the help of Mary:

”I was allowed to take a vow of chastity, poverty, and obedience that I will observe for the rest of my life, and I placed my whole life to Mary’s feet, I begged her to offer my gifts to my Good Jesus and that he may accept me as his bride”.18 Her life changes radically. In four years, she achieves a strong spiritual maturity, truly she can say: “I no longer live it is my Jesus who lives in me.” 19

She wishes to follow Jesus totally: “Oh Eternal Love! You suffered so much for me, grant that I may suffer and die for you.”20

She did not stop, she will not turn back. “Only the Calvary is the certain and safe place where I may find rest.”21

Rosa wishes to give her life to God, and “her blood in exchange for the blood of Jesus.”22

Prayer is her greatest comfort, and her irresistible resource. She used to pray for many hours in the presence of the Blessed Sacrament during the night in her house and also in Church. She often went into a state of spiritual ecstasy when adoring the Eucharistic Host. As a free gift God granted her the revelation of the mysterious “Sign” of the Father’s merciful love.

“I saw the very precious blood of my Lord, and I felt joy. What did this vision make me feel? Oh, my Love, I can only say that you worked a spiritual miracle in my soul, I experienced ecstasy, and I could not say anything. In any case it is very little what can be said to God who is so merciful”.23 Dwelling in God in attitude of prayer and adoration she cries: “What can I do to convert the whole world to you? Oh! There are so many who do not know you, and those who know you run away from you for they did not know you. I would like to go everywhere and loudly calling everybody to come and love you.”24

She becomes a heart that loves as God does “Oh! Why do so many not love you?”

She did not tell anything to anyone regarding her new “way of life”, however her behaviour, her attitude, her inclination to be in communion with God, her desire to assist the poor and the needy revealed it.

3.3 Line of convergence for a new way of life

Rosa participated in various Christian Societies, which during that period were very active in Genoa. These Societies were organized by excellent Priests, who encouraged the promotion of faith in various aspects of worship and of religious instruction and in the practice of charity. Rosa could discover in them an immense field of work: Hours of Eucharistic worship, of promoting the religious press, instructing young people in Christian doctrine, defending “young girls, who were in moral danger” and other works of charity.

Rosa distinguished herself among all other charity workers, for her unconditional gift of her time and efforts, for her perseverance, and for her loyalty to the goal of these Societies.

One problem that interested her, as a mother, closely and urgently, was that of “young girls who were on moral danger”. Many girls came to Genoa to seek work and to escape from poverty.

Unfortunately, many of these girls were young and inexperienced; therefore they always became the victims of dishonest profiteers. It was necessary to use strength and efforts to help them and to save them. Rosa had succeeded in converting her more active and sensitive female friends to this sense of urgency. A small group of “dedicated” Ladies developed, almost all of whom were married, and were also mothers, this became a small Religious “family”, with its regular meetings, ideals, and purposes, and its own Norms of spiritual life. They called themselves the “Ursulines”, according to a custom that was very often used in Genoa, to describe lay ladies who lived in the world, according to a Religious Rule for laypersons.”25

Rosa Gattorno was chosen by all the members of the Society, to be their superior. After one year of trial, the Archbishop, Monsignor Charvaz, officially approved the emerging Association, confirmed the nomination of the superior, and entrusted the spiritual direction of the community to the Canon Fr Luigi Botto. This was at the end of 1864.

In February, 1864, Rosa Gattorno was nominated, by the explicit desire of the Archbishop himself to be the General President of the “Pious Union of the Daughters of Mary Immaculate” established by Fr Giuseppe Frassinetti, with the goal of leading the members, who were remaining in their own families, towards a Christian way of life that was solidly based on spiritual growth and on the practice of the evangelical virtues and of charity. The Union had become widespread in Genoa, and in its suburbs. The same Founder had written and presented the Rule for the approval of the Archbishop. Not having yet received it, asked Rosa Gattorno to mediate, and hoped for a positive outcome as she was an excellent President and because of the high esteem that the Pastor had of her. The Archbishop explained to Rosa the reasons for denying the approval: Some points needed to be corrected and she was invited to her great surprise, to suggest appropriate corrections guessing the points in the Rules the Archbishop disapproved.

She obediently accepted the invitation. In a spirit of prayer and reflection she noted the corrections she understood to be done. She thanked her Good Lord and she continues contemplating the Crucified Christ. At a certain moment she received the inspiration to write something else, something very different. She wrote brief notes of the “Rules for a Monastic Community” then she folded the paper and continued to pray. She did not know, nor did she care to ask what would happen later. The spark of life inspired Mother Rosa in a moment and in an unseen event that she did not predict. This event was beyond her control. Therefore she could not control “when” this happened. Life was born in her, but it did not originate from her.

4. The Work of God

During 1864, while she was a Superior of the growing “Society of the Ursulines”, Rosa Gattorno had reflected about the possibility of following Consecrated Life while living with her own family, harmonizing the family’s needs with the practice of charity works towards others out of her home.

She had noted the difficulties encountered by her fellow sisters, the obstacles, the delays, and the lack of fulfilment in practising works of charity, the lack of answers to the needs of the poor.

However she never had any idea of leaving her paternal home that she now considered to be her home, or leaving her elderly parents and her children.

But the source of life that God had entrusted to her as a gift in that night of prayer demanded the right to be born. She had not withstanding her reluctance to do so, to takes those Notes regarding the establishment of a Monastic Community, and to share them with her spiritual director Father Firpo. What the Spiritual Father told her is narrated in her Memoirs. She was reproached for the delay in obeying God’s will and told her to go soon to the Archbishop. The Archbishop hurried her to “Put into practice the orders of the Lord”, for he could see that the Work would certainly be very beautiful and he encouraged her to write the Rule.26

The Charismatic Vocation

Rosa Gattorno had sought and has obeyed to the will of God when she chose the vocation of married life. And God had blessed her marriage with the gift of children that, according the Gospel she will account for them. Was God now contradicting himself by asking her to leave her children? She now faced an important dilemma. Was it possible that she was receiving a new vocational call from God? Was this “Work” really planned by God or was it a work from the devil? If God wished this Work to be successful was it not possible that another person could do it? In the same enormous sorrow of her mother’s heart, she appealed to the heart of the Holy Father Pope Pius IX. The Holy Father could set her free from that obedience instead He confirmed her that the Work was the will of God! And with enlightenment she also received courage to reaffirm her positive answer of her Christian life:

“I want to do the will of God.”27

4.2 Spiritual motherhood

“In such cruel battle”, she had hoped for “peace and relief” from the Vicar of Christ. “The balm on the wound of sorrow that was bitterly opened” was applied by Mary:

“I prostrated myself at the feet of this Queen, the Queen of Sorrows, and cried bitterly asking her: Must I leave my children? Your Son, in the person of the Pope, orders me to do it. I feel tortured by sorrow; I love them so much…. With whom can I leave them and how? Mary, Mary my Mother, this sorrow reaches my soul… and I remained in contemplation. My tears dried up and I was granted peace and strength in the Most Holy Virgin.

I felt as strong as a giant and I repeated to God with the generosity of Abraham: “here I am Lord I have come to do your will.” 28

At the feet of the Holy Mother, tortured by sorrow, she felt transformed into a spiritual giant and she felt the great peace and joy of her motherhood that brought salvation to all. The human dimension of her motherhood was now opened to a greater spiritual dimension; a gift which she did not seek or wanted, it was a gift given by the pure mercy of God.

In the spirit of Abraham’s faith and of Mary’s faith she participated in the work of the blessed generation that was fulfilled in Mary whom Rosa “loved and venerated”.

4.2.1 Participation in the motherhood - fatherhood of God

Rosa Gattorno could experience the merciful love of the Father with the contemplation of the Crucified Christ, who prolonged his “Memorial” in the Eucharist. In the vision which she saw several times, of Christ’s Blood in the Eucharist that appeared on the Host, she felt an irresistible religious experience. God the Father redeemed her soul through the Blood of his Son and she, daughter in the Son, entered in the experience of the Holy Trinity, which she called “The Essence of Love”. Among various passages of this experience this is very meaningful:

“Oh, Eternal Father! You yourself communicate with me in this communion, by offering to me your Divine Son as you have offered him for the salvation of the whole humanity, so that he may purify all my senses and liberate me completely from their bondage and may grant me your mercy, I am a servant who obeys your will, I always wish to be your servant, grant me fulfilment in the essence of your love. With your delicate hands offer Jesus to me. Yes you are the only Being of my life; you are everything for, when I have you I have everything from you… I have everything.”29

An event has occurred in the soul of Rosa Gattorno. She explains exactly this in her prayer; she repeats in her own way the Magnificat of Mary. The Almighty Lord accomplished in her a great thing: He allowed her to participate in the mystery of Christ’s salvation. She felt unworthy of this gift. In her poor condition of being a sinner, she asks to become involved,”……. Communicate with me in this communion.”, because she yearned to come closer to God, she wished to act as her servant bounded to the mercy of God. She did not desire anything else. She had discovered her beatitude, her sole Good Lord. With a clear awareness she proclaimed her belonging entirely to God: “Yes you are the only Being in my life, you are everything, because when I have you, I have everything.”30

Here Rosa reaches the zenith of her own self-awareness of God: She, who is nothing, receives her “Being” from the Father. If God did not remain close to her, Rosa, her creature would fall into nothingness. She was nothing if she relied only on her own resources; she needed to have the strength that only God can give for her apostolic work. She needed the love and the security that only God could provide. With these gifts she felt completely secure, just as a child in her mother’s arms. For her, God the Father was “infinite justice, infinite mercy, infinite love, the joy of her soul, infinite power, her delight, her shelter, the One who gives everything to me, who stretches his delicate hand over me, he is the guardian and the light of his daughters, the only Being in my life, my everything.”

Mother Rosa reaches to this experience, through the historical stages of her life as a woman: first as a young girl, then as a fiancée, a wife, a mother, and a widow. Which gift did God wish to give to this woman who was fulfilled in her human and in her spiritual life? God grants her his alive personal presence; He helped her, who was already a mother, to become even more active and fecund in the lives of others through her belonging to God, completely to God and living for God.

The “maternity” qualifies the consecration and not only the Mission of her Spiritual Daughters. Their fundamental attitude of believing in the Poor and liberating Christ has its roots in Christ as Son of the Father, who obeyed his Father’s will by dying, and dying on the Cross, because Christ loved his Father. To speak about filial attitude is to speak about the Trinity and the Trinitarian relationship in the dynamic dimension of a love that has the characteristics of Fatherhood. “In the Biblical tradition, God does not appear by only using masculine language; the feminine dimension is also an instrument of God’s revelation.

God and Christ are personified in the female themes of wisdom (Proverbs 8:22-26, Sirach 24:9, Corinthians 24:30) God is also compared to a Mother, who consoles her children (Isaiah 66:13), and a Mother who cannot forget her child (Isaiah 49:15, Psalm 25:6, 116:5). Jesus compared himself to the Mother who wishes to re-unite her children under her protection (Luke 13:14). And at the end of the Church on earth, God will act as a Great and Good Mother; He will dry the tears from our eyes, eyes that are tired from excessive crying. (Revelation 21: 4). Any element of tenderness, of acceptance, and of welcoming, into the final shelter of God’s salvation, is presented in the tradition of feminine language.31

The Saviour entered the human world through the “yes” spoken by Mary; She, trough the mystery of the Incarnation is in an intimate relationship with the Father who, allowed her to participate in His original creative force, and she has also an intimate relationship with the Son who accomplishes in Mary, and through Mary, his historical-human life; Mary also has an intimate relationship with the Holy Spirit who is a divine regenerating force of the human reality of the Eternal Son, in Mary’s womb.32 The Trinity touches deeply Mary: “God has chosen her to manifest the maternal aspect of his person: the generosity, the kindness, the tenderness, the feminine characteristics, the characteristics of a mother. The Virgin is a person in whom the Holy Spirit is present, while the Child Jesus is the Person in whom the Word is present. The two together make the Father’s mysterious presence understandable for human beings.”33

4.3. The dynamism of the new motherhood

How did Mother Rosa live her participation in Mary’s maternal destiny? Mother Rosa was inspired and impressed by “her beauty, and by her power, and by the love she has for us, poor and miserable creatures.”34

Rosa entrusted herself completely to Mary: “Mary, Mary you are my life, ask your servant whatever you will and I will always, always obey you”35 that she may completely and always belong only to Jesus, to be transformed and enlightened by his love. Mother Rosa asked Mary to: “set free from bondage this humble creature …..give me only love! Oh! Become my teacher, and teach me what I must do to be less unpleasant to my dear Lord Jesus”36 Mother Rosa feels to be re-generated in the “Fiat” of Mary sharing her universal motherhood. Through contemplation she clarifies and grows in the awareness of her own participation in Mary’s maternal function in the plan of salvation:

“O Mary, I am saved by you, I am a Religious by your grace, O Mary with your hands you lit the fire of love of your Son in this heart that belongs to your Son. Oh joy! Oh love! Why can’t I die from this joy?”37

From Mary she received the important gift of Mary’s Mother, St. Anne: “I dedicate with great satisfaction, this Work to my Mother.”38 With the Holy Mother she receives the specific Charism, Spirituality, and also the Mission of her Daughters. The Daughters are the historical descendants of the Blessed Family formed of Anne and of Joachim as a sign and an instrument of the Father’s mercy in the motherhood that strengthens, serves, makes life grow and consoles the world.39 In the passionate gift of self to her Good Crucified Lord, accepting the forgiveness and the salvific strength of suffering in the compassion, (to suffer-with), experienced in her affective life and in her flesh, through a “more concrete love” made of actions. It is also tangible and trusting abandonment by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, in the Father’s arms lived through the challenges of suffering and of the “thousand” contradictions of every day’s life:

I offer my sorrows totally to God, and in him alone I lived, me poor slave; It is only my Master, I can assure you that guides me as a child.”40

Mother Rosa lives the dynamism of her charismatic mission with, enthusiasm and with ardour never requited, offering the gift of the merciful love of the Father, gift that was fully manifested in the Crucified Son: to be living only for the Work of God. She wished to belong to everyone, to accept and welcome everyone, with humility and with “limitless charity, and without reward”, with an attitude of peace, strength, and serenity. She made herself available to everyone, acting as a mother. She did this in order that Christ, the living image of the Father, could extend through her cooperation as a mother, her tenderness towards the “dearly beloved” of this world; those who suffer in their flesh and in their spirit, those who are extremely poor children, young persons who experience difficulties, aged persons and everyone else. She also intended to train the Daughters of St. Anne as true active and creative members of the Family wanted by the Father in the Church, helping them to be aware of the vocational charism,; she wished that the family should produce fruits of holiness, in serving and stimulating the growth of a holy spiritual life.

With the heart of a mother, a “compassionate” heart, which expressed God’s maternal tenderness, Mother Rosa wished that her Daughters who would live with authentic hope, hastening and preparing for the coming of the kingdom of God that is the fulfilment of every expectation and the evidence that God’s promise is true and reliable. Mother Rosa reached this dimension of a spiritual motherhood through a process of purification and trial enriched by her conjugal and maternal experience she was harmoniously matures in a new vital and more intensive dynamism. She based her faith on the certainty and trusted in her only Good Lord, the Crucified Jesus, the Being of her life.

RELATIONSHIP OF MOTHERHOOD

The twofold function of motherhood

The intention of surrendering one’s whole life entirely to Christ without any regrets or time limitations: “from this moment, for the rest of my life, your bride only seeks sorrow, and to do what you and the Father wish me to do.”41 For Rosa Gattorno meant that she was constantly aware of God’s will and she was now travelling on the way of uncertainty and adventure, without any fear of experiencing sorrow and the cross.

God called her, to do his Work. Her obedient “yes” confirmed by the Holy Father, Pope Pius the IX, was a pledge that she could not deny. Mother Rosa wrote:

“I repeated the words of Abraham: Here I am, to do your divine will, and I will no longer complain, regret my decision, or hesitate. I offered myself as a victim for God’s Work and I received great consolations, when the most Holy Virgin assured me that she would always be with me, and my children will be her children.” 42

God guided her, with the wonderful pedagogy of love:

“I have been taught by my Eternal Father, and I have been successful in everything I have done according to his will.” 43

And she followed his will she was docile by the grace of the Holy Spirit:

“I can honestly say that I do not feel alive any longer but I live in Him.”44

In this dimension of transcendence she tried to be docile in loving others; she tried to be a reflection of the Father’s mercy and tenderness accepting the littleness of all God’s creatures. What did the Father order her to do? To love God! This love for God that moved her to love her brothers and sisters “was not bound but only a consequence of following the order given to her by God.”45

God was in her heart a source of life for her brothers and sisters. Every day Rosa allowed herself to be taught and guided by the Spirit expressing her gift of motherhood. Therefore, she was able to understand God’s thoughts regarding her own children. At first her children seem to be a great obstacle to God’s call to do his work: “Leave them? It is impossible!”

Can God contradict himself? “Your Holiness, according to the Holy Gospel, God will ask me account of my children!” 46

The Pope’s reply that was interpreted by her in a contest of separation (and it could not be otherwise), had in reality, a meaning that she understood later. “God will take care of your children; you must obey God and do his Work”.47 What a real prophesy!

The love of God manifested in her womb had become a gift of God for her three children. Did the love of God perhaps exclude them from her heart by asking her to achieve spiritual maturity that was extended to the dimensions of the gift without limitations? Saint Vincent De Paul wrote a mild reprimand to Louise De Marillac who was excessively worried about her son’s fate and at the same time believed that she was obeying God’s will, by being too preoccupied with her son:

“Oh, Our Lord certainly made a correct decision when he refused to accept you as his mother, because you do not believe that you obey God’s will, by providing your maternal care, that he requires for your son! Or perhaps you believe that this task will hinder you from obeying God’s will. Therefore honour the tranquillity of the Holy Virgin in a similar case.”48

Rosa Gattorno experienced, as Louise De Marillac did and a few other foundresses of Religious Orders, who were widows and mothers of their own children, the contradiction of the radical change in the direction of her life.

In certain moments especially when the obstacles against the approval of the Rules seemed to be invincible and no one wished to recognize the legitimacy of the Institute’s Charismatic Inspiration, she experienced the temptation of abandoning everything and returning to her children:

“I received it from the hands of God and only one thing saddens me, my children. Gigino’s (Alessandro’s) letter overwhelmed me. Poor me what have I done?” 49

She was also worried regarding the fate of Carlotta and Alessandro; however she never doubted that she was obeying the will of God by being so concerned about her own children. Her mission of motherhood had begun in marriage, had developed through the gift of her own children, and then became extended into a Religious Family, consisting of her spiritual Daughters. Her own children were and remained very important for Mother Rosa.

When she suggested the approval of a new Religious Order to the Pope, her own children were living in an Institution. She did not hesitate to take Carlotta away from the Institution in Piacenza when the manager informed her that Cholera had occurred there. Her heart of mother had already generously sheltered many children, whose parents had died in the Cholera epidemic. Later she sent Carlotta to a boarding school in Milan where an excellent teacher Onorata Colli taught her. Miss Colli was also one of the first lay collaborators in the establishment of the new Religious Family of the Daughters of St. Anne. In the depth of the call to achieve spiritual maturity, God had reminded her to take care of her own children as this was certainly his will. She was certain about this. She expressed her conviction to Maria Adelaide, who was Carlotta’s first daughter:

“You wicked little girl, how can you believe such things? How can you believe that your grandmother would forget you? Oh! You are a strange creature. If only you knew how many prayers I say for all members of my family, how many prayers I commit myself to! So, what should I do? to pray and to write to everybody – first my duty for God’s Work.” 50

Therefore there was a priority: “For the sake of doing the “Work of his heart” I gave everything that I had, and my life itself, in perpetual suffering, and in every kind of sorrow.” 51 However priority did not imply exclusion. Her own children were the children of God rather than only her own children. God had wanted them, He had always loved them in His plan of salvation and He had entrusted them to her. They were also a part, and what an important part! of the petty, poor, ill, life that God entrusted to her service of motherhood.

2. Rosa Gattorno in her filial relationship

To penetrate the “maternal world” of Rosa Gattorno we have reliable and very important historical sources. Among the Documents that sustain our research the most important are the Letters written by Rosa Gattorno to her children, because of their exceptional value. These letters were addressed to Carlotta and her family,52 to Alessandro, and to the Daughters of St. Anne.

Mother Rosa in her letters to her relatives wrote with the strength of her decisive, clear, essential style, and clearly revealed her thoughts and feelings. She was spontaneous, and lively. Her letters were like shafts of light, that not withstanding the distance of time, make her present, relevant, and almost alive today. The letters reveal her feelings, her ideas, her moral character and her intimate thoughts that could be described as a beautiful and immensely rich “house”.

In the far-distant relationship with her children shown by the correspondence, she revealed her ability to love. The care, the respect, the responsibility, the understanding are all characteristics that she displayed throughout her life as a mother. Obtaining access to documents that describe her intimate relationship with her children is a gift for us and a charism; a gift that she was able to communicate to us, a gift developed by her love towards her children and by the power of her love, a power that involves us in its great strength to love others.

3. Relationship with her children

3.1 With Carlotta

There was a relationship based on empathy between Rosa and Carlotta, with profound spiritual resources. Rosa loved her daughter, in the Spirit of her “Good Lord”, and wished that Carlotta would grow free, mature, and blessed by the Lord. Rosa wrote to her daughter: My dear Carlotta, you must love Jesus very much. Allow Jesus to be your sole thought, allow Him to be your beloved husband.” Rosa paid a great deal of attention to Carlotta, and satisfied her petty wishes by granting this wishes: “Tomorrow I will send you the dress that has already been finished. I spoke to your grandfather about a clock and tomorrow, when I will be in Genoa, I will make sure that you will have it; I will take it to you… May the Lord always bless you, always, your poor mother Rosa.”53

The human love of this mother who was “Conquered by Christ,” drew strength from the love of God, and developed a dimension of a motherhood, that was so rich that it embraced the whole earthly life of her daughter. …Attention, time, loyalty, converged towards her, an uninterrupted gift of strength, certainty, love and life. Love and life, these are focal points that existentially united mother and daughter in a continual relationship. Mother Rosa’s letters provide clear evidence of her relationship with her children. The strong and tender expressions used by Mother Rosa reveal not only the quality of the love that transcends life in God; they also reveal that love is strengthened by his paternal and maternal tenderness. But this expression also reveals her concerns, her interest in her real situations, her timely interventions, and the schemes of her maternal pedagogy that was wise because enlightened by her intimate communion with God.

A pedagogy of love that:

Encourages growth

Her daughter did not have to experience loneliness and the absence of her mother. Therefore she made amends for her long absences that were caused by her frequent trips from one community to another with letters and an affectionate dialogue explaining how her activity was different from the activity of other mothers that the young girl could not always accept, or completely understand. Rosa wrote to Carlotta from Nizza on September 7, 1874:

“My dear Carlotta, why are you so disgusted with me? Consider the fact that I am so busy that I do not do anything except writing…I will tell you everything later. You say: poor me, instead you must say my poor mother. Today while I am writing to you I have a strong headache, and I am alone poor mother! Look, you enjoy yourself with Onorata. Be calm, because there is no enjoyment here…

I look forward for the moment when I will leave, I hope that on Saturday I will travel to Ovada; next Monday I will pass through Aqui because as you know, I must speak to the Bishop, then I will not return to Nizza any more, instead I will travel on the same road from Aqui to Ovada. You have nothing to do and nothing to think about, you see everything in a different light…”54

A healthy growth

Carlotta was thirteen years old when in 1867, she was accepted as a boarding guest in Piacenza, and she suffered from deafness that hindered her development of normal and happy relationships. The disturbed and incomplete communication that she suffered influenced her character, often making her moody, aggressive, suspicious, and sad. Once her suffering developed a form that greatly worried Mother Rosa. She sadly described this event to Sister A. Francesca Camisa on 5th February 1869:

”My dear Carlotta has been ill for eight days with a strange illness that appear unusual; my dear daughter acts as if she is mad, and your sister and I cannot leave her alone, and Angiola must also stay with her. Many times, when she is furious not even four of us can control her; she hits everyone with her fists. My Jesus, I assure you that this drink is very bitter for this mother. The doctor assures me that she will be back to a good health and that she is not mad, but at first he made me very worried when he told me that there was a congestion of blood in her brain; now he says that it is the case of nervous irritation. However, my dear Carlotta is not healed notwithstanding many prayers and candles lit for her healing. On Sunday she was so angry that Father Tornatore had to stay here overnight.

What do you think about all these events? Now it is very late, and she has been resting for two hours and occasionally she has been shouting. Last night Father Tornatore stayed with her and I had to constantly stay with her because she was very angry with your sister. I feel ill my vomiting is very severe and I cannot take any medicine. This is my miserable condition. May the Lord be blessed for ever; I hoped to be with you on the first day of her healing; now I cannot say anything else. I will leave as soon as I can leave Carlotta or I can take her with me. She is greatly suffering …”55

During the early years, Rosa took Carlotta with her to various communities when she had to stay for many days in different locations. On 25th August 1869, Mother Rosa writing from Genoa to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, expressed her concern about the minor surgical procedure that “the doctors had to perform on Carlota’s knee,” and advised: “first of all speak about this to Fr Tornatore and ask him to bless her.” 56

Was Carlotta like Alessandro, also predisposed to pulmonary illness? There was an episode that alarmed Mother Rosa and it profoundly disturbed her. She wrote to her son in-law, Gaspare on 22nd February, 1880:

I must ask you to take very good care of Carla who must not loose hope, because the time is coming when she remembers the day that blood came out of her mouth, it is certain that this could happen again. I am very worried.”

The giving of strength

Carlotta’s case therefore consisted of elements that needed to be seriously considered. With good reasons Mother Rosa said: “This thought gives me great sorrow! All these sad thoughts come back to me, one after another!” Her intelligent mind understood her daughter’s situation. She loved, prevented and prayed. She did not emphasize in a dramatic manner the petty gestures that she used to express not to her disapproval, but rather her profound suffering. What passed the heart of a thirteen years old girl, when she saw her mother surrounded by so many young women, whom she loved, served completely, educated, and called them her daughters? What did Carlotta think of Rosa’s decision to leave her in order to follow her spiritual Daughters?

One day while her mother was writing to one of the young women, Carlotta approached her and read: “dear Caterina, my Daughter”. This word is irrelevant, she cannot write this! Was Carlotta not her real daughter? Mother Rosa simply explained to the person who received the letter why the word “Daughter” was scrawled over: “You can imagine over the word “Daughter”, it was my daughter Carlota”. Can Rosa’s daughter take seriously certain statements made by her mother about her relationship with other Daughters, so profound that she dreamed about these relationships? The other Daughters had made a different choice, therefore Mother Rosa told them about the new and wonderful life of the Family of St Anne. From Cento, she writes to the Superior of the community in Piacenza:

“…From here, there are no news, we only need to pray. During this night, I stayed with Daria (the first Daughter of St. Anne, who had recently died in Cento). All the little sleep that I had, helped me to stay healthy, it kept me happy. It was a dream and therefore Carlotta says: these are lies!” 57

It provided understanding and joy

These petty daily episodes not only show, with great simplicity and spontaneity, Carlotta’s latent suffering, they also reveal her firm and resolute character. She was also a Gattorno. In the environment of the Family of St. Anne that contained many positive human and Christian values, she grew as a “good” and “religious” person,” as an honest person, and she learned, by observing her mother with boundless trust, to overcome the weak sides of her personality and to mould her own character, by following her mother’s positive role model. Her friendship with some Nuns was a positive experience for her. She was a friend of Vincenza Rapallino, (the girl that made her angry, when she saw the word “Daughter” in the Rosa’s letter, she scrawled over it). She was also a friend of Benedetta Carrega, and of other Nuns. She enjoyed the friendship of girls who had the education and culture that were suited to her condition. When she revealed to her mother that she had joyfully fallen in love and she wishes to marry the man who loved her, her mother was not at all opposed to their marriage. Even though her mother was anxious about Carlotta’s marriage, she gave her the permission. Rosa’s trusted her daughter Carlotta. Her heart told Rosa that Carlotta would make to be a wonderful wife and a good mother. However, Rosa knew that Carlotta would always need her help.

Carlotta was always affected by her handicap of deafness for the rest of her life and it often had a negative effect on her physical health. Her mother was the only person who knew the real cause of her attitude of pessimism and distrust, often sent her the same message in almost every letter and every possible occasion:

“Be happy! I don’t want any sadness to affect you! Be cheerful my dear Carlotta…my daughter you are so childish, because you worry that I write to Noni (the nice Maria Adelaide), and not to you. Oh! What a creature you are! Do not be disgusted about this; be happy …I do not want you to fell sad, no! no! I say this because sadness is not good, I do not like it.”58 “… my dear Carlotta how can you ever doubt that I love you? Oh! What a strange girl you are! Never doubt that I love you so much. Is that not so? Do you ever see me doing something to hurt you?” 59

Carlotta distrust was created by sadness and by apathy, that could have subtly destroyed her. Her mother stayed close to her with affectionate love of her wonderful humanity and with her gifts of grace. Mother Rosa wrote to Sr. A. Benedetta Carrega in 1880:

…Poor child, one day she will understand the love that her mother has for her. My God, I would feel guilty if I had not done so much to help her!”

The letters that we are examining, and quoting from, were not meant to be specifically pedagogical. They were signs of the love of a mother living far, a mother that was deeply involved in the world and in the field of Work that belong to God, and who travelled and visited the communities of the Daughters of St. Anne. Carlotta wished that her mother’s love should be focused entirely on her, rather than on the Nuns, and she also wished that her mother would spend more time with her. By reading these letters, one may perceive the outline of simple, clear, and consistent pedagogy, that even though was following the married life chosen by Carlotta, was still focused on God, as it was the vocation call to live one’s baptismal consecration as a lay person who centre her life and work on the reality of God’s will.

Guide and sustain

Carlotta as bride and mother had precise responsibilities. Mother Rosa reminds her with sweetness and firm insistence of one who had undergone that kind of experience and not for having heard about it.

Fortunately for Carlotta, the peace and joy that came from the love of her husband helped her to develop a more positive image of herself. We have already seen evidence of this development. Carlotta’s care of her own health was also an important subject. Some quotations from Mother Rosa’s Letters show the tone of her advice:

“…I hear that you are not in good health, what is your illness? Why don’t you eat? Be happy because I will visit you as soon as I can.

I will stay in Naples only a few days; therefore, if you wish that I would come soon and bring a gift for you, I wish to hear that you are eating adequately and that you are increasing in your weight and then you will see what your mother will do…. It seems as if I have not seen you for a very long time…Take care of yourself, let me know if you are eating properly, if you are happy.” 60

“Dear Carlota, yesterday I received your letter with great joy. Thank you, you are a good daughter! Make sure that you look after yourself. I would like to know if you are really healed. Take good care of yourself.”

Mother Rosa did not ask questions about her daughter’s health from mere idle curiosity. Rosa was worried about her son Alessandro who was ill with pulmonary tuberculosis, the same illness that caused the death of his father. Alessandro was very ill in a pitiful condition. His mother wrote, “Even the stones would feel sorry for him”.61 Rosa had assisted him and Alessandro had died one year before this letter was written. Therefore any illness that her daughter suffered alarmed her: “Carlotta, write to me immediately and tell me what is wrong with you. Look after yourself; soon I will be with you.” 62

She wrote to her son-in-law: “Carlotta’s news make me continually upset; it is incredible how I suffer… my God, this is a great sorrow!”63

Later Carlotta was no longer in danger she was healed. Her mother writes these comments on this event: Carlotta, do you understand what has happened to you? Do not strain yourself!” 64

She expressed her concern about her daughter’s health:

“Dear daughter I have received your letter and I understand that you feel anxious even though you tell me you are happy. My dear Carlotta, do not be angry. I wish that you would not upset yourself. Because you may experience again the flow of blood, you know that. Therefore, do not be angry. I hope that you will come soon, is that true? I am waiting for you, so come soon because here (in Piacenza), the weather is no longer hot.” 65

This mother’s care and fear about her daughter’s health may seem to be exaggerated and fearful. However we know that Mother Rosa did not intend to avoid sorrow, and she always believed that it was bearable to suffer for the sake of the love that she felt towards her Good Lord. She confided to her dear friend, the Princess Emilia di Fitalia, on 11th February 1891, from Piacenza, where she assisted her son during the last phase of his illness:

“Sorrows are bearable and one may gladly bear them but anguish is unbearable; to witness so much suffering is a terrible struggle with the humanity that always fights and always wants to win.” 66

She was a mother. She experienced all normal joys and sorrows that all mothers experience. She was deeply affected by the death of her beloved son Alessandro and she decided that it was better not to speak about this to Carlotta because she feared that her daughter would suffer a great trauma if she talked about this untimely death. Rosa wrote to a friend and confided her great sorrow, thirteen days after the death of Alessandro:

”I do not intend to speak about Carlotta. I wonder what my daughter is experiencing, now that she is expecting a child. (Carlotta was at that time in the fifth month of her pregnancy.) She wishes to know everything, she cries, and she worries about her brother; I believe it is better if she does not attend the funeral. I need God’s strength, more than I have ever needed it before.”67

God certainly gave her strength. On her way towards Calvary, the only certain place where she could stop and regain her strength, was her Good Lord, who gave her the courage that she needed to carry on with her spiritual and human creatures God had entrusted to her. He was the only person who could help her and He certainly did so. Mother Rosa was given the courage to bear all the sorrows of her life and to carry her cross to Calvary. Her goodness was unselfish and rather generous. She always took the good care of the persons whom she loved; she knew that this care was not just good during their earthly lives because she was also considering their eternal lives with God. She did not measure time or the sacrifices that she made on their behalf. She gave everything for the sake of God. She always made her efforts for the works of charity with his approval and guidance. She had to help her own children and also to take care of the Religious Family that she had done so much to establish. Notwithstanding the very intense timetable of visits, interviews, and appointments that she had to do she still had time to provide care and joy for her own children and for other relatives. Even late at night, after a day of very hard work she thought of her own family. She remembered them in her prayers and she also wrote about them.

“I must write but I must do it during the night because during the day I have to deal with many persons and with their needs … It is almost midnight at last I can write to you… I am tired I must go now I have little time to write…Read while you can do so I can’t see what I am writing about because it is dark… I can’t keep my eyes open” 68

Rosa’s daughter welcomed correspondence with her mother, when Rosa was absent. Her mother wrote to Carlotta: “I only write briefly to you but I write to you everyday. Are you glad?… Make sure that you use your hearing aid, do not neglect to use it; if you always carry it with you, you will be able to hear properly and you will feel better” 69

In both Piacenza and in Rome the houses where Carlotta’s family lived is suited next door to the motherhouse of the Daughters of St. Anne.

Exhortation and reprimands

Patience, kindness and understanding are not signs of weakness. The gift of understanding the sensitivity that she had developed, the ability to clearly understand the problems and issues and to detect lies, hypocrisy and difficulties was certainly a quality that Mother Rosa possessed and used effectively. She understood her own daughter even more effectively than she understood the mentality of the Nuns. She admonished her daughter firmly but kindly:

“I wish that you would understand the sorrows that others experience! Your own sorrows would then seem to be trivial if you would compare them to the problems of others.”

With a clear insight and with a pure heart she saw the confused thinking of those who attempted to turn her daughter against her: On 29th October 1882, she wrote to Carlotta:

“Dear Carlotta,

I have received your letter and I hear that you are not happy. Why? Do you say that you fear my anger, why do you say that? For what reasons do you suppose that I am angry with you? I am always thinking about you, I am even attempting to find a baby carer for you. What more could you ask for? I know that no other mother does for her children what I do for you, so why do you have so many doubts? Any one who tells you that I do not do enough for you is a liar or his mind is confused by prejudice. Be happy I find that I have serious thoughts because I am in debt and without a great deal of money. I must undo many things… do you understand what I am saying? It will be easier when I explain everything to you directly. Your affectionate mother must now say goodbye.”70

During twenty-two years of marriage, Carlotta had six children. Such numerous fairly requires constant attention and efforts. Carlotta needed a great attitude of sacrifice to cope with this situation. When she was forty-three years old she felt exhausted and without faith in her future. Carlotta revealed her discouragement to her mother. Mother Rosa understood Carlotta’s situation. The problem was not really Carlotta’s children who were so full of life, friendly and a blessing from God. The problem was different and Mother Rosa revealed its nature:

“You are wrong when you say: many children no. God does not like it. You have to be happy, take out as a temptation the thought of not having enough money. This is what a greedy person does. I never think that way while the Institute has many needs and all the Sisters I have to maintain; is it true? You too, be abandoned in God he will think to all your needs. Will you do it? So be happy.” 71

Completely abandoned in God. This is the secret of the spiritual fecundity of Mother Rosa: God thinks about everything for having chosen the Good Lord as the only necessary. Could her daughter understand it and live the same ideal?

Rosa repeated this subject in another letter, but she did not wish to influence Carlotta because she trusted her daughter’s understanding. Rosa’s strong belief was expressed in love and meekness:
