“….think that mammy is all for her Carlotta. Every time she need and when you want something you have only to tell me and you will get it, believe me. Provided that it is not against the equity because I know you very straightforward and you are able to do only good. Brava!” 72

Mother Rosa knew how to stimulate the best thoughts in the human soul and how to unleash authentically Christian thoughts:

Dear Carlotta,

Yesterday I wrote to you, now I am again writing to you. Be happy! Will you promise to be happy? You must not think about anything, instead you must put everything into the hands of God. I promise you that Jesus will always take care of his children. So then do not complain! Woe to those who complain! Be happy….”73

Thinking is equivalent to worrying excessively about the future. This is an anti-Christian characteristic; it is a typical attitude of those who lack faith. At this point Mother Rosa outlined a spiritual plan for her daughter, the same plan that was prophetically indicated by the unforgettable Pope Pius IX:

“God will take care of your children, you must take care of God in his Work.” The Pope’s prophecy was completely appropriate for Mother Rosa and she assured her daughter: “Your mother promise that Jesus will always take care of his children!”

3.1.1 With Carlotta’s family

Mother Rosa had wished that her daughter would follow her example of Religious Life. To offer her own daughter to Jesus as an intimate gift from her mother, to offer her “little girl’s” spiritual life to the only Good Lord, to have mother and daughter united in his infinite and merciful love both being dedicated to him, to serve God in his Work, was indeed a great dream! The mother tried to enlighten her daughter’s future with this spiritual life. For Mother Rosa who had experienced the dizziness of mystical love and endured the most severe penances that sought a spiritual way of greater love towards God and his creatures, it was a normal desirable way of life to follow the only Good Lord. She told her daughter:

“Carlotta, you must love Jesus very much, let him be your only thought; my daughter allow Jesus to be your beloved husband.” 74

Carlotta formed a relationship with Caterina Rapallino, a young postulant, who was then living in Piacenza; Carlotta confided in Caterina and during the early times seemed to share Caterina’s ideals.

Carlotta said,” I feel that my heart is joined to Jesus.” Carlotta admired and felt a great sense of solidarity with Caterina. Also she sent this message to her. “You are brave Caterina. You are very brave you wish to become a Nun not to marry” 75 Caterina wished to become a Daughter of St. Anne, but because of her poor health her parents refused to give their permission. After four years she finally succeeded in being accepted by the Daughters of St. Anne.

When Mother Rosa communicated this news to Sr. Francesca Camisa, referred precisely to Caterina (who was now Sr Vincenza), and to Carlotta, the two souls that were taken care of with great predilection but were still distant from fulfilling Mother Rosa’s great expectations. Rosa expressed her thoughts in this way:

“For them Jesus remains on the Cross all day long because they do not wish to be on the Cross and they do not wish to carry it and they leave it completely on his holy shoulders. Therefore I have thought of carrying the Cross myself and of leaving them on mount Tabor. They become true disciples by eating only sweet! I must be strong enough to carry the cross I desire to spend Eternity in paradise by the grace of our Bride Jesus.”76

However Carlotta clarified her own intentions and her expectations. She greatly enjoyed the friendship with the Morazzani family, whom the good Onorata Collli had allowed her to meet. Their kindness filled her with joy. She discovered a more beautiful and attractive world by attending the theatre (with the permission of Fr. Tornatore) and she also participated in family parties and learned how to dance.

Her need to love and to be loved, to be with persons whom she could trust to have secure relationships was fulfilled by her great friendship with his family.

Eventually Carlotta’s need for a positive relationship led her to meet her “wonderful prince,” Count Gaspare Barbiellini Amidei who came from a noble Roman family.77 Their marriage was celebrated in Genoa, on 23rd April 1876. It was a blessed union and it generated children. Mother Rosa was certainly optimistic about the future of the new family.

With her son-in-law Gaspare Barbiellini Amedei

Mother Rosa welcomed her son-in-law, and treated him as a son. She wrote to Alessandro from America a short time after the marriage ceremony and expressed her feelings: “I assure you that now you have a true brother and when you will meet him you will love him.” 78 Mother Rosa believed that her daughter had found an excellent husband. She contributed to the spiritual welfare of both husband and wife, with her prayers, wise advice and with any possible and necessary intervention. She helped to strengthen the positive spirit of the new family. She wished that the new family would live in mutual love and respect and with love to God. Rosa knew that Gaspare loved Carlotta and that he was worthy of respect and esteem. She knew that he was very honest. Their friendly and sincere relationship between Rosa and Gaspare developed in this positive way from the beginning.79 It eventually becomes a relationship of family love. Nonetheless Mother Rosa provided more realistic comment in her letters:

“Dear Gaspare,

If today I would have not receive a letter from Giuseppina, and from Superior informing me that you are in better health, it would be horrible day for me but the dear Lord Jesus was kind and He answered my prayer; may he be praised forever, I know that you are feeling better. For God’s sake take care of your self” 80

You cannot imagine how delighted I was for your letter that confirms you are well. I thank God for this. Why do not all of you remain in the countryside for a holiday? It seems too much trouble to come and go for Carlotta’s…” 81

“Dear Carlotta, Nonny and Gaspare,(at the last place is always the most important person) I wrote to you yesterday; today I am writing again, tomorrow I will not be able to write because I will be very busy. I wish that soon you will announce that you have received my letter where I told you about going to Firenze…”82

“Listen Gaspare I want you to write to your uncle and you must do this for my sake. If it is true that you love me as a mother, then you and Carlotta must write to him immediately…” 83

This uncle to whom Mother Rosa refers was precisely her brother Federico, a Senator of the kingdom of Italy, who was very influential in both Rome and in Genoa.

In the more delicate situations Mother Rosa always consulted her son-in–law. She wished that her daughter’s health should be good by preventing Carlotta from becoming aware of any message that could have upset her.

“ … Listen Gaspare I am telling you to keep this topic as a secret, for God’s sake I repeat, you must not allow Carlotta to read letters that contain sad news, because sadness is a poison for her. If she becomes upset, her health will suffer and then I would be very worried. Soon I will arrive…” 84

Each member of the family had his or her own responsibilities. Maturity consists of giving one’s love with mutual respect and care. Her son-in-law relayed much on mother Rosa. During critical events such as illnesses the words and the good advice that was provided by Mother Rosa became the most effective remedy and provided a strong dose of optimism.

“Listen I am certain that something bad has happened to poor Rosetta..85 Just as an illness happened to me when I was ill again in Pistoia and the second time was worse than the first time. So she should apply “Milan’s fly” medicine on her chest that will do a great deal of good; she should drink milk, great quantity of milk; her coughing is also a dangerous symptom. This is better than an illness, but make sure that she does not travel by train because it is unhealthy for her to do so”

“After this illness is over, she may do as she pleases, but for the time being she must not strain herself, for her health’s sake. Finally she must stay in bed, or at least seated, she must not become upset, she must not worry, I entrust her to your care.”86

Carlotta was preeminent in the thoughts of both M. Rosa and Gaspare. The love that they felt for Carlotta influenced them towards developing the greatest respect, and the most intensive attention towards Carlotta.

“I entrust Carlotta to your care, because she is close to the time of delivery… do not leave her alone, ask if there is a good midwife …prepare everything that is necessary, because I am worried about it. Tell her to be happy, because three saints have told me that she will have a very pleasant deliver…”87

Rosa and Gaspare also tried to help Carlotta with all her family tasks and duties:

“My Son,

I write to you now, I have received your letter, and Carlotta’s message; they fill me with great joy. I am sending a small parcel, filled with pine-nuts, and sweets. I know that you need some toys for your daughter, be patient, one day I will send them.

I cannot send the carpet, be patient I will tell you about this later. Dear children, you can’t imagine how busy I have been, especially when I was in Rome, where there was so much work to do. So be patient, because I can’t do anything more. I do the work that even a giant could not do. Oh, Yes! I can do all my work by the grace of God. Tomorrow Sr. Benedetta will send so many toys that you will be satisfied, perhaps they will be even too many.”88

These letters speak alone; they allow us to understand the intimate thoughts and feelings of this healthy family which was inspired by Christian principles. They also show unedited aspect of M. Rosa an exceptional lady, not only as a mother, but also as a mother-in-law and as grandmother. Below we have an expression of her feelings, in a letter written to her son-in-law, sent from Paris, dated 2nd June 1888:

“Dear Gaspare,

I look forward for the time of my return and I hope to travel the later on Wednesday, because I can’t wait any longer. I assure you that I feel so sad, so sorrowful, because my work is becoming exhausting. I am now 57 years old, and my request for funds and for other forms of assistance are very long and very unpleasant indeed! Oh! I wish I could fly; I would like to fly with one leg! However… I hope to travel on Wednesday away from this terrible…I will tell you about this late. I hope that you have received my letters; be careful make sure that the children are not sunburned. Here there was a very bad case of sunburn. For goodness’ sake make sure that they wear their hats. I hope that nothing bad will happen to them! I say goodbye to Carlotta, tell her that I will be with her and that I will be with you soon.

Goodbye. Your affectionate M. Rosa. Give a kiss to the children.”89

Holiness makes one capable of the greatest and most positive gestures, because it liberates one’s heart from every type of hypocrisy and selfishness. Holiness arouses and sustains thoughts and feelings of goodness and of altruistic attention towards others. The presence of M. Rosa was a blessing from God that strengthened her children’s love. She was greatly comforted, when she could see their mutual love. To gain a more accurate knowledge of the persons whom M. Rosa loved especially Gaspare, we quote here from a letter, written to her son Bernardo, which was written many months after Carlotta’s death:

“Dear Dino,

Allow me to tell you something, I don’t feel calm, I suffer from your mother’s absence; everything makes me feel sad, I think about the fact that I cannot think about anything now. My Grandchildren behave with courage, but I don’t know how my children behave (….) when we are alone I can speak; I don’t know what I should say in the presence of others and I feel sad that I can’t confide in you, as I did with your mother. All of the rooms remind me of Carlotta, and she is present at least in my imagination, she was so happy about the house and I believe that her spirit would suffer, if I sell it (…) Be patient and understand how much I suffer for the lack of the companion who was the centre of my life.”90

Gaspare and Carlotta did not experience conflict in their marriage. They were very fortunate, because they were deeply united in their love and their children and because of the valuable presence of M. Rosa, on whom all of them could rely on for advice and support.

She was a stable and secure counsellor, not only from a human point of view. Her spirituality left traces and good example that could be followed by anyone. Solutions based on love were developed by M. Rosa, and relationships were important, the members of the family cared their everyday spiritual life. This was true even though they experienced problems.

Pedagogy of involvement

After Carlotta’s marriage, M. Rosa saw marriage from a different point of view in relation to one’s husband, to one’s children and to responsibilities that derive from marriage:

“I desire many blessings, I wish that you will spend one hundred years in happiness with your dear family (…), I always pray for you, I think about you and your family.”91

She wrote this message to Carlotta, for Carlotta’s saint’s day. To Gaspare she sent this message:

“Yesterday I received an audience with the Pope, and I spoke to him about Carlotta, Pupa and you for a long time (…) You will hear news from me.” 92

M. Rosa was certainly not lazy in giving her energy totally to the Work of God and in helping her own children even though her work with the Daughters of St. Anne was rather different from the work she did for her own children. Her children lived both spiritual and secular lives. She always thanked God for having taken her away ‘from the noise of the world’ and for having sent her to the house of the Holy Mother; she thanked God for her children who were called to follow different vocations living in the world; she prayed for them and she was for them a sign of God’s maternal love with her meaningful and positive actions. She was always active in her love and care with her own strength and devotion to the Lord Jesus; she carried her Cross of love and of sorrow. She believed that the constant self sacrifice of her own life and her everyday efforts to help others, were of little value as far as good was concerned.

However, Carlotta, Gaspare and their children, certainly understood the motivations that were behind her actions. They also understood the motives that were behind their own actions. M. Rosa made this point clear in her letters:

“You feel sad because I don’t write to you my daughter. But what can I do? If only you could see all the hard work that I have to do! If you could see it, you would certainly say: my mother is right!” 93

And again

“Dear Carlotta,

Yesterday I wrote to you, and to Maria (Maria Adelaide her first grandchild), I am waiting for her reply, she should not become angry. Poor mother, everyone wants me to do everything, and I can’t, I must go for one person and visit others. I am old and I must move slowly. You must be patient if I have come here (in Lercara), they have sent me here. And what suffering have I endured? You live a sheltered life. I can only say that this work is of little value for the Lord Jesus.” 94

She tried to involve them in their mission as much as possible she could. She told her son-in-law, and her daughter who now had three children, in 1881:

“I must tell you some good news I have agreed to take care of a nursery school. Oh! What a wonderful place it is and it’s so neatly organized. If Carlotta will see it, she would like it very much: thirty-two sleeping cots, all of them set in neat rows. I will tell you about this later. This provides a great deal of work for me I must do everything, but we are in a positive situation. (…) You may imagine we must organize all the seats of equipment in Corso Street, in the warehouse. All the children must be dressed in white, the fabric of excellent quality, I will tell you about this later.” 95

To make the burden of her absence easier to bear, she kept her relatives informed about her activities as we quote from this letter:

“… I hope that I may leave on Saturday, I will stay overnight in Girgenti and tomorrow I will leave again, I will stop in Rossano then I will spend two days in Naples then I will be with you. You see, I have to sign a contract in Girgenti, and then I have to sign a contract in Rossano. Do you understand dear Carlotta? But you will be very happy.”96

Only a holy mother could live with such intensity Jesus’ Commandment: “Love one another as I have loved you” Yet her relatives were not happy! How could one express the feelings, that were expressed in a letter written to Gaspare from Paris, a message that seems to contain clairvoyant thoughts: “There seems to be a conflict between us“. What did her relatives not understand or wish to understand about M. Rosa? In his biography of M. Rosa Father Fiocchi clearly speaks of ‘great expectations and material advantages concerning the financial resources of the Institute.97 This is an issue that should be clarified elsewhere. We are concerned with merely mentioning it by using the written primary source that exists. When she was confronted by the requests made by her relatives, M. Rosa was severe and firm as her replies to Maria Adelaide her granddaughter confirms:

“Yesterday I received your letter, and in Adelaide’s letter, you always complain poverty. Oh! I really don’t know what I should say. Be patient about money. You will believe this, but I sent 200 lire to you, you must examine your accounts and then tell me if I did send the money, or if I did not. I don’t have a great deal of money, so what can I do if I don’t have them? I can’t take money away from the Institute, but I will help you in any way I can, even if I have to endure poverty…” 98

To her other granddaughter Maria she wrote:

I have received your message, you ask me to give to you money that belongs to the Institute. I can’t do that, God Himself orders us that we may not steal what does not belong to us.

Your affectionate Grandmother, M.Rosa.”99

Living as the children of God consists of truth, of actions of rules: these are necessary, because love must always accompany the truth. To educate, to develop to achieve spiritual maturity, to provide a precise direction, without compromises, is difficult and also costly. Rosa who was and who wished to be a mother in the complete sense of motherhood knew how to use every opportunity, even an opportunity provided by a mistake, to completely rectify the direction. She was vigilant and careful. Her love towards her children had this creative dimension, nourished by God’s mercy.

With her grandchildren

At the age of 46, M. Rosa experienced the consolation of holding in her arms, her first grandchild, Maria Adelaide. She was so happy about this event. Carlotta’s motherhood had the same roots as her own mother. The birth of new children was a sign of God’s mercy and of his loving care towards the new family. M. Rosa admired her grandchildren with wonder; she felt that they were an intimate part of her own life. She understood the profound sense of motherhood: a new welcome and a gift, the capacity of loving in different type of love that was more tender and sweet, understanding and indulgent; she also felt a new desire to allow herself to be strengthened by these new lives, which were the fruits of her own children’s lives.

Her relationship with her grandchildren had these fundamental qualities. To the very good education provided by their parents, she added her effective spiritual and human contribution with a positive influence that was understood by her grandchildren. Her wise advice formed a goodness and honesty in their hearts. Here is some evidence of this development:

“Dear Maria Adelaide,

I feel that you are working as a woman in cleaning the house; you act as a young grandmother, well done!

Your affectionate M. Rosa”

“Dear Nini

You will always look after your father, you are already so thoughtful. Well done! Jesus rewards those who love their parents very much. So be careful and don’t harm yourself in the sun at sea, but enjoy yourself.

Your affectionate Grandmother Rosa.

A kiss to the little girl.”100

Maria Adelaide, Carlota’s first-born child was her grandmother’s favourite, because she was so wise. A profound relationship allowed both of them to open themselves to understanding, to welcoming, to a happy family life. In a letter written just before the feast day of St. Anne, in 1883, she invited her with gentle insistence, to visit Piacenza:

“Dear Noni,

I don’t know how to live without my Noni. What are you doing? Aren’t you coming for St. Anne feast day? Come, you will see so many beautiful things, what a great feast day it will be! Dear Noni, come so that we will be together. I feel really sad because you are alone. Detta and Giuseppina remember you. Detta remember you and says that she would like you to be here.

Goodbye, goodbye, please come. You affectionate M. Rosa”101

In another letter, she sent her a rather happy greeting for her Saint’s day;

“Dear Maria Adelaide

You are grandmother’s favourite, long may you live, long may you live. I also wish to clink my glass, to wish all your family happiness, I can almost see you from distance, all of you are united and happy, here I am holding Beppina who is also drinking to your health. The weather is becoming cool and cloudy; I also have other news which I will tell you soon.

Your affectionate M. Rosa”102

M. Rosa treated Maria Adelaide with great respect. She was pleased with that child who did not disappoint her own expectations, or the expectations of her parents; she knew that God blessed her granddaughter.

“Dear Adelaide,

I can’t wait more to hear that you have done everything, and then I will take my hat off to you, and I will call you Countess, my young mistress. All right dear Maria. Oh! What a terrible time this is for me. Calumnies against me are vibrant! Today I have started a three-days prayers for my opponents. May Jesus give happiness to them just as much happiness as the sorrow they have given to me. My soul rejoices because it gains spiritual merit. My poor body weakens and feels ill. I greet everyone. Console me with good news, my mistress. I remember you with love,

Your affectionate Grandmother Rosa.”103

Nonny had also become an adult, she was 19 years old, and now this was an appropriate time for M. Rosa to speak to Nonny rather seriously, to reveal some information about her own life to allow Nonny to understand how the ability to endure suffering for the sake of loving others, generates forgiveness based on love; a forgiveness that inspires positive feelings that helps one’s spiritual happiness. To her adult, but still young granddaughter who contemplated a future of happiness in marriage, she could provide no greater benefit, than the certainty of the Good Lord who is infinitely superior to any other lord: the love of two mothers who are unique in the world who provided a true promise of great happiness:

“Mother, mother, grace is vigilant, she guides you and loves you, the Holy mother and the most Holy Virgin Mary protects you in a very special way.”104

The very special love for these two heavenly mothers was real and visible in two earthly mothers: Mother Carlotta, and Grandmother Rosa.

M. Rosa and her grandchildren: here is an intimate family portrait, which reminds us of G. Giusti’s poem: “At the cradle, in sweet act of love”

“…The little girls are always here with me. I do not leave them alone, until they sleep in the evening. Tell Carlotta that she must remain cheerful. Nonny is in good health; Rosetta is ill, but not seriously. Rosetta is happy she is enjoying herself, she seems to be in perfect health. In any event, I am here to heal her. Hope that her minor illness will soon cease.”105

The images and actions speak for themselves. No comments are necessary for describing or explaining dimensions and the quality of motherhood for M.Rosa Gattorno.

3.2 With her son Alessandro

When she wrote the history of her decision to establish the Institute, many years after this events had happened, M. Rosa decided to write about the difficult decision to leave her children. She traced the outlines of a symbiotic history of her relationship with Carlotta and Alessandro:

“What in fact happened was that the Holy Virgin Mary specially protected them, wrapping their souls in her Holy mantle, so that they could bear my absence with courage and strength. I was not at all worried about their education because God made special provision to take care of them through the help of many kind persons. My son sometimes was involved in a few scrapes, but he never frequented bad company, it all was happening because of his good heart; but he was coming back and doing his spiritual exercise with the Friars. They used to praise him for his love towards me, he has always loved me; for him I was the centre of his life, when in boarding school someone told him that I had become a nun, he was very upset, he could not think coherently for a few days. I approached him dressed as layperson, as soon as he saw me he stared at me then said, Mother! Mother! How can I describe this event? My soul was breaking but I forced myself to appear calm, so he did not notice that I was upset. I forced him to think, I told him that I was dressed as a lay person because I was not yet a nun, then he looked at the ladies who were already dressed as nuns, and he wept. Suddenly he became very angry and he wished to strike me, as he did not realize what he was doing. Then I thought of taking him with me, (as he was not yet eleven years old), and with kindness, I took him to retreat with me, then he received his first Holy Communion so well that it was a consolation, then he returned to boarding school and was giving signs that he wished to become a priest. His confessor told me that every day he received Holy Communion; the confessor also informed me that he stayed in constant contact with him, because he did too many severe penances, so the priest was worried about his health. During that time I took my Vows as a nun, he wept when he saw me, but he did not make a scene.

I realized that I am out of topic… and I feel confused and perhaps I should not narrate certain details. Only God knows how much sorrow these events have caused for me.”106

Unfortunately Alessandro was deprived of his father, who died when Alessandro was three years old. He was also deprived the intimate and long-term warmth of family life, and of constant direct contact with his mother.

As Alessandro had a good, a very sensitive personality he suffered very much because of their absence. When he was nine years old, his mother sent him to a boarding school in Genoa, which was managed by the Sons of Mary Immaculate, so that he could receive good accademic and Christian education. During the 19th century, it was the general custom of the Italian middle class to sent children to a boarding school. His mother in addition to his relatives, and teachers, tried to create a group of friends, who were seriously interested in his growth: Father Accinelli, his spiritual director had a long term friend of the family, Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, Father Tornatore, who loved him as a son, Father Agostino Donadio, the good Onorata Colli and other good friends.

M. Rosa entrusted Alessandro to Sr. Camisa’s care:

“I entrust to you Alessandro and everything that you do for him I consider a great favour to me. May God reward you for your kindness.”

M. Rosa wrote this letter from Foligno in 1873. She made this point clear in many other letters but she was responsible of her son and she never delegated this task. Even though she was far from him, and busy with many tasks demanded by the Work of God, nevertheless she was close to him as if he was her only child. Her son listened to her advice and he was glad that his mother cared for him. He wrote to her:

“Poor Mother, what a good person you are! However you should think about your health that is not good. Think about the fact that you are everything for us, not only as mother but also as a spiritual guide. As I have not been fortunate enough to know my father, I have concentrated my love completely on you; therefore I have united the good that I would like to receive from both parents, to one parent alone.” 107

Alessandro receive a reply from her mother, to both his verbal and to his silent, questions, he also received material help and spiritual help, and the strength of love that revived his courage and hope. His wishes were to be successful in his studies to follow a worthwhile career in society, to work to honour his mother.

The interrelationship between mother and the son who shared so many ideals notwithstanding their different vocations is narrated in their letters that they exchanged during their lives.108

In boarding school

During the period if his cultural education (for various reasons, Alessandro studied in four boarding schools).109 M. Rosa followed his education with great interest. She was happy about his efforts in study. His good behaviour, his efforts to succeed in his studies, seemed to guarantee a positive outcome for M. Rosa. However, the boy found life in a boarding school to be oppressive. The strict discipline, his homesickness, the absence of his Psychological and physical illnesses caused much suffering for him. His mother was attentive to his situation and frequently he sent him messages, messages that reflected her love: “I feel much the sacrifice of leaving you, but I am very happy, it is a consolation for you.”110

The letters that his mother sent to him encouraged Alessandro to live in hope:

“You and your sister should write more often” Her visits were joyful events: “As you are in Sampierdarena, come and spend a day with me, as you have promised.”111

The boy frequently asked for pretty gifts, such as toys, or pocket money. His mother always granted his wishes, directly or through relatives or friends. She was always vigilant and she understood when her son was physically or psychologically ill. With the passing of the year, she realized that her son’s life was changing; she understood that the negative influence of some of Alessandro’s schoolmate was having bad effects on his behaviour. She intervened providing wise advice and she forbade him to frequent certain schoolmates.

However her son was no longer docile, although he was always respectful towards his mother.

Alessandro now reasoned with an self-standing mind, and made his own choices for bad or for good. He decided to abandon his classical studies (he was never very successful in classical studies), and chose to prepare for commercial studies. To do this effectively he needed tutoring in Mathematics and in Accounting.

In search of work and…. Fortune

It is clear that his family tradition certainly influenced Alessandro’s choice of a career. He was eighteen years old, he did not wish to be a burden to any one, he sought his place in the world and he contemplated immigrating to a distant continent, America. His mother was saddened by this decision and opposed his desire to emigrate. She wrote a severe and precise letter to Alessandro, providing advice that was sensible and that would benefit him:

“My dear Alessandro,

I have received your letter, you can’t imagine how much sorrow it has caused me; I am not allowing you to migrate and I will never give my approval. Listen make sure that you remain a Christian and that you stay away from bad companions and make sure that you go home early in the evening. For goodness sake Alessandro, I advice you to leave your companions: when they tell you that I can’t support you, tell them that until now you have not been supported by anyone, except by your mother and she will always help you. You will find work one day, make sure that you speak to the Magnini family, by nagging them they will decide to employ you; astonish everyone by enrolling in the Congregation of St. Vincent! You must know that I spent a long time in that Congregation, the Lord will grant to you the favours that you ask from him, I don’t have any other Lord than my God, I have everything from him.

You see how His grace towards me continues! Ah! My dear Alessandro take heed of my advice, ask the Lord to help you and you will have what you need. I am waiting for you to tell me that you have joined the Congregation. What a consolation it would be to see my son helping the poor. It would be a wonderful consolation for me. That decision depends on you.

Your affectionate Mother Rosa.”112

M. Rosa also tried to convince her relatives to help Alessandro. Was it possible for Alessandro to obtain work in Genova? Mother Rosa wrote to her very trustworthy friend Sr. A. Francesca Camisa:

“Listen I wish that you could spend a few days in Genoa and observe how Alessandro is and at the same time go and seek Mr. Magnini, that gentle man who was ill, whom we visited together and ask him if he has found any work for Alessandro, by doing this you will also hear what my mother has to say. Do you know what Alessandro wishes to do? He is planning to travel to America. Can you tell me your opinion? What a strange plan it is! I am concerned not so much about Alessandro’s bodily health, but rather his soul. If he migrates to America, I am worried that his soul should be thrown into that abyss that contains so many forms of anti-Christian heresies; these heresies are the beginning of hell for a poor young man who is not experienced in the ways of the world and who travels into that abyss! I am afraid for Him! Don’t let Alessandro notice that I have spoken to you about this matter, but listen to what he will tell you and then you will reply by listening to the Holy Mother’s thoughts.” 113

Mediation was done in vain. Alessandro believed that his mother’s reasons for opposing his plan to migrate were based on excessive pessimism. Her son who trusted his mother so much and who had always obeyed her wishes did not abandon his plan. The young immigrant dreamt of becoming wealthy and noble, and nobly dreamt of being helpful to his dear mother. He travelled to Piacenza to comfort her. He explained all his good reasons for his decision to migrate and the reasons why his mother could forgive him for making that decision. He assured his mother that his adventurous journey towards the unknown country of Argentina would always feel her presence, he would always love her. He sent his mother this message: “Now more than ever before, I feel the need to love you and to console you.”114

He wrote this message from Cadiz, during his journey. When she could no longer be in direct contact with her son, she felt that she would be separated from him forever. She felt the most pessimistic premonitions. She wrote in her memoirs:

“Today my son came to say goodbye, as he was departing to America. The sorrow that I felt was caused by the thought that I would never see him again, this thought made me feel very sad. However the saddest thought is that Alessandro could encounter a bad fate in those very deprived countries, and if he unfortunately dies suddenly, where would his soul go! I say this because he would certainly die without receiving the spiritual comforts of the church, certainly not as a good Christian. He would forget my God! Then would loose him for all the eternity! Oh! What a terrible sorrow I would feel, if one of my children dies outside the presence of my God! Should I believe that this would be a thorn in the heart of my Good Lord? Oh! What have I done? I can’t stand this sorrow.” 115

In the apex of her sorrow, she invoked the Virgin, the Mother of her Good Lord, who was also her mother, and the mother of her children, so that she could help her to redeem her son:

“Oh! Sorrowful Virgin you agreed to act as his guardian, when he was a young boy, will you allow his soul to be lost? Oh my love! My son’s soul! My sorrow increased. My God I give everything to you. Save my son’s soul. I was so shaken, that I experienced many tribulations, so many that I felt weak and ill. I was so exhausted, that I went to bed late during the night without receiving any relief or comfort from another person. I was alone!” 116

Alone with her Good she suffered, and she implored him to fulfil her motherhood: the admittance of her son’s soul to heaven.

“Oh, my love! Have mercy on him, hold your son close to you, heal him and don’t let him move away from your side, this is the place where I hope to see him safe in your arms, safe for eternity. Oh my sorrow, mixed with the love of my Good Lord, makes me experience such peculiar feelings, that I can’t describe these feelings.”117

She finally felt that her son, who was the subject of so much of her sorrow, and so many of her prayers would be saved. Her Good Lord assured her about this. We read in her memoirs:

“My Good Lord comes to help me, He calmed me. He assured me that my children would be well…. They will be safe, He will never abandon them, and he will guide them in every aspect of their lives. Oh! I can’t describe the peace and joy that I felt, a peace and joy that I felt constantly. Even I would experience the greatest sorrows these would not affect me at all. Oh! When I think about those words, that I have done the will of God, everything seems to be good and every sorrow is delight. Oh! My love, how can I thank you?”118

God’s plan for her own life was unfolding itself, in the solar clarity of the mystical gifts, as a wonderful free gift of love that involved M. Rosa with the whole human race, in all countries of the world. She had no longer one life, but many lives to generate.

In the dash of love that unites, she a little nothing felt immersed in the force of the Spirit and repeated the “yes” of the unconditional gift of motherhood.

“What can I do? Nothing being nothing even less than nothing. I can do everything only if am strengthened by your force. Oh! My Love, how can I be quiet without allowing everyone to know who you are!”119

The young Alessandro, in leaving everyone he loved, and his entire world, was animated and motivated not only by the mirage of gaining fortune and better future. The hidden force of his mother’s prayers strengthened him in the depth of his being. He faced difficulties that he had never previously experienced:

“I sleep in a hammock (inside the shop), wearing my day’s clothes and I have stack of news papers as a pillow; what do you expect, these are the living conditions that exist in America. But don’t worry I will achieve a successful career.” 120

The hardships of sleeping on a hammock, continued for these three months then Alessandro decided to live in a rented room. Now he confessed to his mother:

“I am paying for the sorrows that I caused for you, with the life of deprivation and work that I have. I work from Seven o’clock in the morning to Ten o’clock in the evening. However, except for the fact that you are distant from me, I am happy. I eat by working with my hands.”121

Therefore he worked hard, he wished to be worthy of his mother to help her to understand the advantages of his sojourn in Buenos Aires. On February 2o, 1876, he wrote to his mother, and conveyed this information:

”I have been thinking that your nuns should come to Argentina;

I feel that they would be welcomed and accepted very well. I know the deputy secretary of the Archbishop, who is a very good person and has so much influence… I hope that the next ship bring a letter from him, or perhaps from the Archbishop himself. Therefore you should be glad that I came to Argentina, so that with my petty assistance, you may be able to expand your Religious Order throughout the world…”122

He regarded this matter as being urgent and he was very interested in it’s implementation. In the following letter he made these comments:

“I spoke with the Archbishop’s secretary; in the meantime you should make sure that your nuns learn the Spanish language.”123

His mother was very enthusiastic and did everything that she could do to help Alessandro. Fortunately we still have a letter that she wrote to her son during that period:

“My dear son,

Onorata told me that this is a good occasion for writing to you. I am taking advantage of this occasion; dear Alessandro, you should realize that your poor mother would like to have an everyday occasion for writing to you; I have given 40 Franks to the person whom you mentioned. Consider that I would like to see you having a good career and I feel sad because you are always wandering around and you are no longer living with your cousin. Never mind!

I hope that you have received the linen with the other goods that your uncle and aunt sent to you; you may sell these goods, they have also sent some magnificent wine, and a magnificent clock. You may see how much we are thinking about you, we have not forgotten you, notwithstanding your complaint. No, no! We haven’t forgotten you! Ah! My God! If you could see how many prayers your poor mother has said and still says for you, you would not have any thought that may disturb you, you must not think that I have forgotten you! Ah! My dear son, one day you will understand that we love you ask me about the furniture; your uncle and aunt say that the furniture may not be suitable for you, because it is too expensive, therefore it will not be useful for you. I have sent the linen to you immediately, I hope that you find the goods that your uncle and aunt sent to you to be useful. Don’t feel lost and discouraged if your cousin’s financial affairs are not going well, because you will understand that money can be easily earned or lost, but the rest of our lives that is health can be lost and never regained if it is lost. Therefore, look after yourself and consider that everything on this earth ends and only good and evil remain for us to eternity, good will give eternal life to us and evil…

Well! I don’t even wish to think about the evil because this is a sorrow that makes me die if I will not see my dear son for the rest of eternity. Will I not see you for the rest of eternity? No, no harm will come to you, our Lady will keep him safe, I will enjoy his company forever; your sister is still living in Albaro with her husband. I assure you that he is a good man, you have gained a true brother when you will meet him, you will like him, I warn you that I am very much in debt, but by saving some money, I hope to pay debts and to help you, by sending to you what you need, but now I feel certain that you will be sorry for me, is that not true? Therefore be patient, I hope that you will be satisfied with what I have done. Goodbye, dear son, the Father sends his regards to you. Goodbye, I embrace you;

I am your very affectionate mother, M. Rosa Gattorno.”124

The son valued the wealth of good advice, of spiritual life, that his mother gave to him. “How could I not listen to your advice, every word seem Sacrosanct”?

However, he was really lonely in that distant country and his odyssey (adventure) went from bad to worst. He wrote to his mother:

“My cousin Emmanuele has experienced such a serious form of bankruptcy that if he lived in Europe, he would be imprisoned, he deserves to be imprisoned, but he is a freeman and pays all his debts.”

Alessandro needed powerful friends and substantial source of financial assistance if he wished to be successful in commerce in Argentina. Conclusion of his odyssey (adventure): In December 1876, Alessandro had returned to Genoa again, he sought work… and to earn a fortune. Notwithstanding the financial loss he was sustained by his mother’s spiritual strength and his, by his trust in his mother’s constant love, he hoped and attempted to find constructive work.

“You letter was a great consolation for me, it is good to hear that you still love me.” I am waiting with great impatience for the day when I will be employed, by accepting employment in the bank, I am making a sacrifice for two years, then I will certainly have a good position in the society.”125

Months passed in his vain search for work that was honest, dignified and that was suitable for his expectations, and for his aspirations. Alessandro patiently bore having to continually ask his mother for money. He needed a health cure on the seaside and Don Accinelli gave to him the money that was necessary, but not enough money for prolonging his sojourn that was beneficial for his health. He needed an overcoat and a hat, he wished to pay rent for a room that he could get a way from his aunt Emilia, who allowed him to live in a room without natural light, he wished not to be the target of criticism, as his grandmother and his uncle Checco, “Waged war against him.” He recited a litany of needs and complaints to his mother who tried to help him. However, he was aware that his son behaviour was not good. He told her “If I could be a consolation for you!” 126

Alessandro always had weak health; at various times he had been seriously ill even when he was a boarding student. It is easy to imagine the sorrow that M. Rosa felt. M. Rosa herself revealed her secret to us, a deep “sorrow” in one of her touching and eloquent expressions that come from the heart with a unique urgency: We find this in a letter written on September 1877 to Sr. A. Benedetta Carrega:

“I received the latest letter from my aunt that told me that Alessandro is feeling a little better, but he was in danger of dying and I had already sacrificed him to God. He is my son! You can’t certainly realize what this sorrow means to me, it is a deadly agony. There were moments when I felt that my body was detaching itself from my soul. Oh! What a great sorrow! My God I did not believe that in this world, one could experience such a cruel sorrow. I am a mother! I have abandoned them to serve God, but I tell you I am a mother!”

After such a great confusion, finally she experienced a glimmer of hope and clarity.

The adventure in Florence

The promise of employment in a bank in Florence was finally fulfilled. Thanks to his mother’s friends, the young man was employed by the urgency of the industrial Sub-alpine bank He was welcomed as a son of Rosa Gattorno, should be welcomed with an open heart, esteem with a clear pleasure of doing something that pleased his mother. Alessandro spoke in a humorous manner about his two friends: “Andreotti looks like Josaphat’s trumpet, mother, Oh! Who has influenced him? I will not speak about Monti and his wife: You are their God.”127

Preceded by good reputation of such a great mother, he had to behave properly moral rectitude, irreproachable behaviour, and an honest way of life was expected of him. Unfortunately, he had to wait for some months before he was paid his wages. In the meantime, he had to ask his mother for money; in every letter he asked for money, with humility, good manners and legitimate motives. He experienced debts, problems, and financial misfortunes. His mother, who knew the dangers that he faced, suggested that he should think about marriage. This suggestion hurt Alessandro’s sensitivity. He certainly thought about marriage! Why did he go to America? He was in love with Miss Marazzani! He was still thinking about marriage! He was certainly in love with Countess Ruccellai. His mother took the advantage of this occasion and suggested that he should think about asking the young Miss Ruccelai to marry him. Alessandro was realistic and told his mother:

“She is a countess and her family has high expectations if he marries. She is a serious obstacle. Therefore, one must not speak about a possible marriage between her and me. Dear mother, you are deluding yourself. A man who is wealthy may expect to marry her. I am poor so must forget her.” 128

As usually did Mother Rosa approached him for the sentimental side:

“You are a continuous sorrow!”

This sorrow became a deep wound, when during a very long conversation with the bank manager she learned a dishonourable fact: her son was living with a bad woman and he had abandoned his work without a good reason, he behaved badly. He was living with one of those bad women and he introduced her as his wife. Alessandro had decided to ask for a transfer to Rome.

“How I suffer! I experience the pain of hell; this is the greatest sorrow that one may experience. I have never felt such a great sorrow! Oh! death is as nothing when compared to this sorrow, no sorrow is greater than this.”

Why had her son deceived her in such a shameful way? She suffered great sorrow, but her sin was her son’s sin, rather than being her own sin. This had to be healed. It was true that he behaved immorally, but because of his weakness and of his excessive goodness. As she had always done in the past, she had to help him now.

Alessandro healing and his “own” business

Towards the end of 1879, Alessandro together with Maria Tellini the lady whom he had married in the spring of that year and his son were living in Alatri, in the province of Frosinone. In this town, he developed a small factory that made cement and oil. His mother’s forgiveness had been his salvation; just like a raft can save a shipwrecked sailor. The lessons that he had learned from his mistakes made him prudent, his misfortunes had made him more mature, he was now more inclined to be sensitive, his feelings were deeper; he developed a sense of the religious meaning of life. His letters to his mother, during this period are like an echo of her teachings. He opened his heart to God:

“Dear mother, I would like to give to you many consolations and to be useful in a field of work.” But how happy I would be if I could see dear Maddalena as a happy person, I wish to be useful to her! I hope that God and our Lady will grant me his favour.”129

His mother’s goodness also had a beneficial influence on Maria.

“She has become a very good person, thanks to you. Both of us have returned to the good Jesus, like good Christians. Poor Maria! She had not a family who loved her, not even a loving father or mother.”

The mother was happy for her son, she waited together with her son, and she now knew that there was bright future of hope for all the family. His sins had been healed.

“Alessandro has really achieved a good position in the society. He is married and has a son. He is so good really religious and he is a good example for everyone. He has established a good business and I hope that he will not need anyone’s help, in a few years from now, he will be able to help others because he is very generous. I hope that God will bless him and that he will help him to do everything well. You should also pray for him.” 130

Her son continued to give consoling news:“The factory is going on well and everyday, I am making progress.” But he also talked about travelling, of business deals, of his worries, of all the problems that he endure in order to achieve the position that he wished to have. He made many mistakes. Perhaps he lacked an understanding of business methodology, of how to achieve a successful business. His dreams were not all peaceful! He asked his mother for advice as if she was commercial consultant. She realized that she was being used in some way as an instrument. She revealed her feelings to Sr. Benedetta Carrega:

“I enclose a letter from Alessandro who is always in the same situation! O cross, cross you are really pleasant… Everyone lies and acts like hypocrites131, there is no truth from anyone: I have become used to lies, they can’t hurt me any longer, you know what my only comfort is.”

Alessandro felt sad about his mother’s failure to reply to his letters, as she usually did and also because he worried her:

“You are certainly upset with me, because I asked you for advice. But listen dear mother, every time that I must make a decision, I sit at my desk and I question you in your portrait. I discuss matters that affect my business, because I believe that you can hear me. So dear mother if I ask you for your advice in so many business matters is because when you say: Act according to this method I feel peaceful,

I am not afraid of making mistakes. So forgive me if I have caused sorrow to you, it was not my intention to do so. But it really seems impossible that I could not be the cause of sorrows! I say: my Lord Jesus, I ask you to be good, yet I always remain the same; you don’t know how crushed I feel by sorrow, I fear that you are ill… you can’t imagine how much this thought crushes me. But the only person that I have in the world is you. My wife and my son are very dear to me but they can never be the substitutes for my mother’s love. Now the factory is going well; I will write to you, to keep you informed.”

Unfortunately the slow progress of the new factory, turned because of mistakes made in its administration and ended in financial disaster. On October 1, 1882, Alessandro was in Rome and he found accommodation in a rented room. Dedicated to his plan of not causing a new sorrow for his mother, he wrote to her:

“Dear mother, do not worry about me, everything will be resolved. Consider your health that is the only subject that concerns me; the other subjects will be resolved. So my dear mother don’t feel sorry for me don’t think and worry for me you will see, Federico will resolve all the difficulties.”132

A new intervention.

His mother, in agreement with her brother Federico, found an immediate solution for the problem: Alessandro had to transfer himself to Genoa. He obeyed and did not become discouraged. The courage that he needed to restore his business to good fortune and to withstand the benevolent or perhaps intolerant opinions of his relatives and of his friends came from his mother, “she was genius who has achieved so many positive results, and who has achieved a high position in society.”

When he compared himself to his mother, he felt so petty and needed her almost constant support; notwithstanding this, he loved her and wished that she should be happy; he wished that she should no longer have a reason to complain about him.

“My poor mother even though have so many worries in your convents, and your numerous financial affairs, you still remember your son and no one knows how many hours you exhaust yourself in work, instead at the age of 30, I am still a burden to you and who knows for how long. However my mother, believe that I do not miss any occasion for improving my situation, but for now I feel like a little boy, I fall without your help. My will to work certainly exists and soon if nothing else happens, I will return to Genoa, with a greater will to succeed, to makeup for the time I have lost, and I will work.”

His new activity in Genoa was a small shop that sold goods in partnership with Mr. Rapetto. His mother also gave him various tasks: purchasing fabrics, or pasta, or other goods that her nuns needed. She did everything she could do to deserve his trust. Reflecting on the immense love that his mother expressed, in a thousand ways, his love and esteem for her grew and increased. “Which lady is stronger and more virtuous than my holy mother? Your son does not fawn on you, because you gave to him not only life but with your virtue, you have helped him and he is proud to have such a mother.” 133

Not withstanding his weak health, he was involved in a great deal of activity. But, eventually, he became dissatisfied with this activity, and urgently asked himself if he should continue with this activity, or he should follow a different path. He still felt attracted to America not by the mirage of earning a great fortune but with the prospect of a stable and secure business activity.

A decision that brought salvation: Gargatano

Therefore, Alessandro explained his plan to his mother, explaining the motivation for his decision with an objective judgment about his unsuccessful results in commerce, which unfortunately were repeated. He wrote to her in Genoa, on 11th September 1886:

Dear mother, thank you for the concern in replying to my letter. I regret very much that you don’t agree with my opinion, yet I know that by thinking about it you will change your mind.

Listen I have tried many paths and I only lost money. I know that I have decided to travel to America Oh! I did this after a serious reflection. I know a good commercial trading company that trades in America, which would like to employ me as a representative. I have a friend in America who writes to me, he has told me that if I wish to work there, I would find work with a good reference from Mr. D’Arci who manages the railway that connects Bolivia with the pacific. Over there, I don’t have the kind of life that I almost have to live here, so you can understand that it is better if I leave. After all, what can I do here? Nothing, other than spending and loosing money, I don’t ask for anything when I leave, only my family is important to me and I hope that you with your generous soul will believe that this is the right decision… Now then dear mother, think carefully that I am still a young man and still have sufficient time to make a good career for myself in America.” 134

This time his mother was clearer than ever before in her opposition to his plan. She did not change her mind. Alessandro did not leave. His mother made sure that he would have worked in the farm of Gargatano. And at last her son truly saw the possibility of relieving her from a burden. He collaborated with his mother for the achievement of his great work, that is her glory and therefore, a good reflection on her children who are proud of having a mother who was certainly rather different to other mothers. 135

During this period he still managed to hurt his mother. His mother became aware that Carlo, who was introduced by Alessandro as his son, before his marriage to Maria Tellini, was in fact not his son. He confessed this with such repentance, that his mother forgave him unconditionally. He had another reason for reforming his life. Remarking on this event, he wrote to his mother a few days later:

‘I understand how stupid I was because I did not confide in you, if I had confided in you before, now I would not be in this situation. But from now on my mother, you will be my confessor.”136

In the same letter he writes about his new tasks in his work, he had to plough, sow, harvest, fertilize his crops, and buy some domestic animals. He also talked about his health, he suffered from severe cough but that was nothing to worry him.

The last destination

Alessandro was never in good health. He had been seriously ill many times. On July 15th 1887, his wife wrote to the superior, Sr. Santina da Gargatano:

“Alessandro’s health is not going well. Since last Saturday, he has suffered from a very high fever, above 39 degrees. Dr. Albertazzi believes that this fever is caused by a lung infection. He has lost great deal of weight; it is pitiful to see him.”137

In other subsequent letters, the news was better. The same doctor, a short time after this event, assured his mother that “It is not this illness that Alessandro had.”138 It was clear that the illness was present. The same illness became fully developed a few years later, with great strength.

Father Tornatore who was in Piacenza was close to Alessandro during this period. He acted as a friend and a father, more so now than ever before. He prayed to the Sorrowful Lady and to the venerable Father Bernardo Maria Clausi, so that the son would be healed “in body and soul” and carried in his heart the burden of sorrows of Alessandro, and of his distant mother, a point of reference for both a force of hope, I accepting and living this sorrowful reality and this extreme sorrow. He often visited Alessandro, he often wrote to his mother. At the right moment, he warned her to go and see her son, because he was terminally ill.

“Alessandro is desperate to see you before he dies because he must tell you important facts concerning his financial interests in Gargatano. Behind these petty words, I have begun to suspect that Alessandro wishes to discuss legal subjects with you I also believe that his confessor has ordered him to discuss these subjects with you. And for this reason Alessandro must speak to you. I have told you my suspicion you do what God inspires you to do; for goodness sake if you are not feeling well don’t travel during this harsh season. Let’s hope that God will allow him to live until you are able to travel.” 139

Having been warned by telegraphic message sent by Bishop Monsignor GB Scalabrini, the mother reached Piacenza on January 20th 1891, to be with her son. He was a son who caused her much sorrow and whom she loved so much. She saw her as unrecognizable person, defeated, a skeleton, a martyr who was on his way to death. Everyday, from seven in the morning to seven in the evening, she was with her son, in the house on Bishop House Street where he lived. She did not neglect the work of the Institute, but she also wrote letters in the dying man’s room and the work that she could not do during the day she did it in the evening. The unpublished details of the last two months of Alessandro’s are revealed in the letters that M. Rosa wrote. In every letter, “Poor Alessandro” is mentioned, she only used brief words that described the stark reality and reveal the feelings, fears and expectations that she experienced.

“Dear Emilia, how terrible it is to see my son who is dying. I can’t recognize him, he does not speak, and he is a poor man. God give strength to us, to him and to me. His resignation goes beyond that a nun can have and he is of good example. Everyone was amazed, even the doctors. When I asked him: “are you feeling better?” he replies “May God’s will be done.” “And he feels better, he eats soup.”

One day Alessandro seemed to be dying, and the Holy Oil was given to him.

He asked everyone to call his mother; she rushed to see him at one o’clock in the morning. Now he could leave this life with his mother who accompanied him. However, his time had to come. He had a slight reprieve.

“He speaks about death as if speaking about a walk, he prays, he is worried that he will not be patient. Oh! How is this city inspired by this example! The doctors watch over him and are moved. Oh! What a miracle that our Lady has done? The ill man suffers greatly. He is experiencing a real purgatory and those who assist him suffer even a great sadness. The sorrows that he experiences are terrible. He is a skeleton who inspires sorrow. My God have mercy! I can’t say anything else. The poor man suffers so much! Only the morphine injections calm him and when he wakes he feels better. He says that he wishes to leave! What a bad clue! Two hours ago he called me to tell me that he wished to dress himself, and to walk down. Can you imagine that! He is a skeleton.

What a sight! May everything happen according to the will of Jesus! Poor Alessandro, he is deteriorating as each hour passes. For fifteen days he has not eaten solid food. He only takes liquid nourishment. It is terrible to see him dying. The ill man also suffers from a painful leg. He cries and says: Our Lady, My Lord Jesus, I can’t stand this pain any longer. Even stones would be moved for him. He is now like a skeleton; he is so thin that the doctors don’t know where they can inject him. The doctors don’t understand how he is still alive. It is a great sorrow! What can I say? This has been decreed, we must say: God’s will be done! As for me, I know that I deserve everything!” 140

At this point in any moment, her son can only wait for eternal life. She reviewed the past… she relives it. She remembers so many events! One day Alessandro had written to her:

“I have my mother who loves me, who is happy with me, what on earth can I desire now? God and our Lady should grant me one wish, that I should go to heaven when I die, because I will meet my father there then our dear mother will see us there (…) I ask our Lady to make me a saint.”141

Alessandro’s silence became more intense. He was involved with his own self; His mother felt that he was losing his battle to live.

“He can’t even swallow water. It is sad to see him, since he seems to be dying. Oh! What a great sorrow, dear Celsa! How badly ill he is! He is far away from everything, he never asks about anyone, since the day he received the last sacrament he is calm and does not care about anything.”142

On March 16th, the last day of Alessandro’s life, she stayed near her son, since seven in the morning. She looked at him with pity and love. She felt very sad. “How strong is this sorrow!” 143

But she did not cried for she was strong and her son did not see her any longer but he died alone. And she could not stop him. At five in the afternoon, he entered eternal life. He was now in his Father’s House, in the Father’s mystery of mercy. Now he could rest. She went to her room and wept and the Sisters heard her weeping for hours. Was this weakness? No. The mystery of death was lost in the obscure universe. She touched the purpose of life; she experienced the fullness of love, which was deeply affected by the event. But there in the depth of God, her son was given back to her eternally alive.

“Poor Alessandro, he died.” -She writes after some time to Princess Fitalia- This was a great event expected by the priests themselves who assisted him and someone came to see me and said: Oh! How great and powerful is God’s mercy! Saint Joseph visited him and took him away during his Novena.”144

Alessandro was alive; he was in God’s presence. And from this presence, her motherhood gained new dimensions of Charism.

With “her” Daughters of St. Anne

A point of reference regarding the choices that were made by Rosa Gattorno, was “The will of God”. In obedience to God’s will, she had chosen married life; in obedience she made her exodus, moving away from all her security, following Christ’s will. She left in opposition to the demands of her parents and of the demands of her heart. Her parents claimed the right to keep her in Genoa, the right of having her filial love. However, she left the family and her city Genoa as a response to a strong call to follow God’s will. She left behind all the past.

On 12th March 1886, she arrived in Piacenza with five companions. The Work of God would have its origins and its roots in that city. She did not yet know “how” this would happen. She only knew with a deep interior belief that the reason and the purpose of the Work of God was only He: her Good Crucified Lord, of whom she was the poor servant, chosen because of God’s “pure mercy”.

She was a servant who needed to be moulded, so that she would not hinder and not ruin everything. She had to leave her own desires and follow him, she had to allow herself to love and transform herself, until she become totally immersed in God’s will. She walked with Him and for Him and accomplished God’s will. The foundation of the Work was her death in Christ, so that she could rise again.

“My Crucified Lord, lords her humanity gives strength and energy, he strengthens the spirit, that reigns over all the powers, that are conquered: One’s pride is destroyed, is lost… pride has been defeated. My Crucified Lord has replaced my will with His Will and it is infinitely sweet and pleasant not to posses it any longer.” Oh, how I would have rebelled, if he would have not nailed it even though was left free forever!”145

4.1 Wealth of the source

In her exodus of obedience to the Father, she always sought a union with the Crucified Christ and participation in the grace that was given to her; she would be a disciple and a faithful bride. She conformed to Christ’s will.

“I was very shapeless and He, with His Grace made me beautiful, by giving His grace to me; he took away the old creature and of a gentle one I was dressed.”146

She became a reflection of Christ. Her personality was emanating a strong, unexplainable force that attracted individuals to do good deeds and to make coherent choices to follow a Christian way of life. Mother Rosa wrote:

“Oh my Love, what do you want me to do? I don’t now what else I can give to you, because everything that I have is yours; I no longer have my own life; I can honestly say that I don’t feel alive any longer, but I live in Him.” 147

This was the source of her great spiritual motherhood.

4.2 The Daughters in the Spirit are born

The first five Companions who left Genoa for Piacenza with M. Rosa, (Three of these left the group, because they could not adapt to community life). Others soon joined the new community, with great increase in number.148

When M. Rosa died in 1900, there were almost 4,000 nuns. Many Sisters declared that they decided to enter religious life, in the “Daughters of St. Anne” because moved by the “fascinating” witness of the Mother. One of her looks, one of her words, her person had a prophetic effect: she revealed the message of God’s presence. Because her way of life, expressed the work that God wished to do in his creatures, the creatures that he loved and that he called to follow Him closely.

An anthology of episodes of her “vocational intervention” that were extended even after her death from the simplest to those that have the characteristics of being extraordinary events would enlighten some very interesting vocational stories. We limit ourselves in remembering the experience of two of the first Sisters who were so dear to the Mother and who worked so hard to assist her in the new Work: Sister Francesca Camisa and Sister Vincenza Rapallino. The encounter with the Mother and her unusual call and their response, is told in the brief “Life of Francesca Camisa.” 149

Francesca with her mother had travelled from her native city, Cortemaggiore to visit Mother Gattorno, and also her own sister Luigia who had been a Daughter of St. Anne for four months. They spent a long time on a friendly conversation and Francesca did not decide to leave; she seemed to be held there by an unknown force, but it was very powerful force and she could not resist it.

Francesca was asked to leave by her own mother who was already walking away from the Convent. Francesca was also walking away from Mother Rosa’s presence when she heard these words: “Frascesca do you want to abandon me?”, which Rev. Mother Gattorno told her. Francesca took her veil covering her head and gave it to her mother and told her: “Mother I am staying in this community, because I feel that I cannot leave it.”150

The meeting and the vocational call and response she made were different for Caterina Rapallino. M. Rosa certainly knew her in Genoa before she established the Community in Piacenza. Caterina had been entrusted to M. Rosa’s care by her parents, who hoped that the climate in Piacenza would be beneficial for their daughter’s health, as Caterina suffered from bronchial asthma. Caterina had been previously sent to other healthy places but without any positive results. Caterina discovered a new mother. She felt at ease, she felt as a full member of the community, she felt as a participant in the affairs of that new family. She worked closely with M. Rosa, “Whose presence comforts my heart so much, I feel happiness, a kind of happiness that I have never felt before… it is happiness that I can’t describe.” She sent this message to Cento. 151

An intimate relationship based on esteem and love developed between M. Rosa and her spiritual daughter. Caterina felt the strong call that came from Jesus to be a member of the Daughters of St. Anne. However, her decision to join was delayed by the opposition of her parents, and by various other obstacles. Mother Rosa supported her vocation and also encouraged it. Even though she respected Caterina’s freedom to choose, Rosa became the voice of her conscience. On 23rd December 1868, M. Rosa wrote to Caterina:

“You have told me that I should leave you alone, because you always feel that a voice is calling you. Ah! My Daughter, I am not calling you, but the Lord Jesus is calling you, He is afraid that Caterina will betray Him, and He is calling you; How will you reply?”

M. Rosa took on herself the burden of that weakness. This weakness was similar to the fear of the cross. She prayed and suffered. The Daughter became attached to the love of her spiritual Mother she would find the strength to say “Yes.” In a letter she told her:

“Oh! How much will Jesus reward you, if you will be able to give this soul to Him. I completely entrust this soul to you! Yes, all the merit will be yours! My dear pray that you will not become discouraged, if you believe that, I am careless and indifferent, a voice inside me tells me that your wish will be granted.”152

But years passed before the wish of both of them could be fulfilled. On 9th December 1869 M. Rosa told Sr. Francesca Camisa:

“Finally the devil has lost the soul and the Mother St. Anne has now one more Daughter. Now there are five Daughters of St. Anne (this is the number of the first nuns), but one of these may be called the Daughter of miracles and of sorrows, this is Caterina. Now if you write to her, call her Sr. A.M. Vincenza.”

Relationship of “filial” Motherhood

In Piacenza, in the house of the Holy Mother, the New Religious Family was being established; Rosa the Mother of her daughters who, having left everything for the sake of obeying God’s will, stayed with them and guided by her they were seeking only God. Rosa was living in the two wonderful presences the one of Christ and the one of her Daughters.

The centre of the house was Jesus in the Most Holy Sacrament. He was the Magnet who attracted M. Rosa and everything in her: her heart, her thought, her feelings derived its meaning, its light and its energy from him. Her life was a perpetual contemplative prayer, a mystical condition, a fervent wish for a deeper presence, which was stronger than any other presence. It was the earth-possession of her Good Lord, full of charity, a fertilizing grain of life.

Her life was the womb for her Daughters, who like her had been called by the Father to do His Work that would have to develop into a huge tree: “the kind of work I am asking you to do will be great” In that adjective, “Great” is the only form of light received. M. Rosa did not know how and when this Work would have developed; it was slowly going manifesting to her by the Holy Spirit her Governor, through events, unexpected events and the challenges of daily life.

The Work needed to have secure foundations and secure structures. She had the young women who established the new Congregation with materials needed for the starting of this Work. Each one was to be built on the “Corner stone, which is Christ” to become “a living stone” of the harmonious unity according to the plan of God in the dynamic force of the Spirit.

M. Rosa welcomed them and looked after them with an intelligent method that was based on faith, a faith that was enlightened by the heart. She discovered their gifts and their spiritual wealth, the good qualities that should be developed, their limits, their secret sorrows. In each nun, there was the mystery of the Work to be fulfilled.

In them takes form and her new maternity acquire meaning and shape in the certainty of the charism.

Mother Rosa tenderly and tenaciously loved them. She felt that they belonged to her, but not in an exclusively meaning of possessing them.

First of all, before being her Daughters, they were the daughters of a jealous God, the Brides of Christ and the Daughters of the Holy Mother.

She directed them towards the “Centre” of mutual love. She told them: “Remember that you belong to God and that you always belong to me”.

“My God, you must steal this heart, so that it may be filled with passionate love; because, it will never be able to love, if it is outside the centre of your heart; Saint Anna, you must become part of that heart, and make it love your nephew, Jesus.” 153 “You may be sure that this poor mother left you in a corporal sense, but spiritually took you away to take you for ever inside the heart of Jesus, so that in a real fusion of love, you will forget this miserable person and you will seek to find her and to see her near the Eternal Father… May God bless you and may He pour on you torrents of His Grace, and may you become a true daughter now, but I wish that you will become a better nun.” 154

My dear, don’t believe that I am distant from you because I feel closer to you than if we worked side by side with. I think about you every minute and my thoughts are about you; I always pray to God that I will be near to you; you see, my beloved Daughter, consider that it is convenient that I should solve the problems that exists here because when my work here is finished, I will come to you and I will stay with you for a long time. Come on, reflect on this and you will understand that this is God’s will for His Work.” 155

In Him she embraced her:

“I can only embrace you in the heart of Jesus, so that you may be consumed by His divine love.”156 “I Always keep you close to my Jesus and I tell Him that he may help you to develop a faithful obedience to the holy Rules and that He will Make you a true Daughter of St. Anne, then finally you may die in His Love. Oh! Dear Daughter, if you will enjoy the fate of receiving a small part of this divine Love, you and I; believe that I am yours close to my Crucifix.”157

Her maternal love was meaningful, because it derived from her Charismatic vocation, it was expression of a love that was given through the gift of one’s self to God and to the Daughters of the Spirit.

This love-charismatic-gift, through its experience and its personality developed peculiar qualities of maturity, fullness and of tenderness.

The Mother had already dedicated her whole being to be with her Eternal Father in obedience to the Spirit, by following the Crucified Jesus. She did this because Jesus had revealed to her and had communicated to her the depth and the immensity of the Father’s maternal love in the position of the arms that were nailed on the Cross, wide opened in an attitude of accepting all people, and acceptance that was given as a free gift: “Come to me all of you.”

To hold these Daughters close to Him is a gift of participation in this immense love. This “ardour” of love that was experimented in the intimate contemplation of her Good Lord in the daily relationship with the Daughters, was expressed in the nuances that are appropriate to maternal love: satisfaction, worries, understanding, forgiveness, constructive feelings, of the tender protection of those who know how to be close and rejoice about the revelation of the love of God, that enlightens so well, sustains and protects his creatures.

“May God be blessed because this time I can hold the pen to write to my Daughter to show to her how happy I am about her good progress; even though my bad health and my immense activities do not give to me a moment of rest; even though I wish to leave everything apart for a moment and I want to express my feelings in this message because our Eternal Father has taught me that one must experience benevolence to those who deserve it, just as one must whip someone when it is necessary to do so.”158

“I hear about what you have done, I approve of everything and I am very happy about your work. I bless God because he has enlightened you so well.”159
