You will not believe this, but this is how you act, you don’t know that a quantity is derived from little, you are still inexperienced in household management and you don’t know this language, because you are young and you are not used to household management but your poor Mother is old and she knows these subjects well, she sees them and is disgusted because as we live by providence, we must be careful about everything and then our Holy Rules impose this.”257

To live by trusting in the Providence without stable income, exposed them to uncertainty, to anxiety, to worry, above all where there were many people to support. The Mother helps to establish the necessity of today and of tomorrow, not on insecure human hopes and security, but on God the Father.

“Let us confide in God, and He will provide because we are doing His work.”258

“I’m joyful that God sent a little providence to you; let us thank our dear Treasurer. I wish to know if you have paid the chemist and how much you owe to the milkman and about the other accounts. Let us pray to the Lord, so that He may send providence to us and let us never loose courage, we always trust in God’s mercy, we do not stop doing it.”259

On 21st April 1877, she wrote to a Superior:

“To pay your debts, you save excessively, even to the point of taking away what is necessary for you and for others. Therefore, leave, abandon this bad practice and start to buy meat, milk, wine in the quantity and quality that is required by a community of people who work so much as you are. Therefore I hope that your will do this immediately and we will pay the debts; never doubt this.”260

The Mother understood, intervened and freed everyone from all kinds of fear. But she demands faith in God:

“I feel compassion for you but I don’t like your discouragement, because it belongs to worldly persons who don’t have faith in their God because they don’t know Him, and they have little faith in Him.”261

“Be brave, don’t worry, God will do everything. Those who live for Him are certain that He will defend them.”262

“Be brave, Jesus will always help you. Therefore be brave and write to me. Oh! Yes, you will see that the Lord will send his providence to you, and you will pay your debts, and then you will be free and you will be able to have food and drinks during the winter such as potatoes and wine. It would be wise for you to buy grapes and then make wine at home. What do you think of this?263

The Superior must have the personality of a strong woman and a spirit of sacrifice that can withstand any trial.

“Let us work now, and then we will have a blessed rest. Be strong my Daughter, don’t fear; this poor Mother will always be with you whenever you go. Make sure that you stay close to God, and you will have everything.”264

“When I see what you do and you act according to what God inspires you to do, I feel an immense consolation. Be brave, one must be strong during difficult times.” 265

“Be brave Daughters, go forward without fear, Jesus likes generous souls. Always give good news to me they are a real comfort to me. Oh! My God, bless my dear Daughter, so that she becomes a model that God’s Work requires.” 266

One emerges strengthened from trials and struggle and becomes aware of one’s responsibility as a spiritual guide of the Sisters and of the economic administrative management of the community. One becomes an effective instrument of God in His work, not sustained by one’s own merits, but by the grace of vocation in the Family of the Holy Mother of Mary Immaculate, one plays one’s role with maturity.

The Mother says this in different ways and at appropriate times. She sent this message to Sr. Biagia Pedroni who was concerned about the financial affairs of the community:

“You say that I will approve your accounting. Listen, do you know what do I do with the accounting? I don’t care about this subject, because this belongs completely to one’s own conscience. When a Superior knows that she manages resources that belong to the Lord, she must care for them. Is that not true? Your conscience is accountable to God.” 267

It was part of M. Rosa’s pedagogy to warn the Superiors about their mistakes but she did this with a great degree of discernment!

“My Daughter, don’t worry about what I have written to you, because you must know that I am not disgusted with you, no, my Daughter, you must understand that my advice is not a reprimand, it is a suggestion, all of my advice is given for your own good and for the good of our dear Institute. Is this true? 268

She also made sure to express her approval and praise: Well done! You have done everything well. I am very happy,” and other similar statements. She expressed approval, sharing of joy, in an increase of tenderness:

“It is not necessary for me to give advice to you being already aware of these matters. Well done! I am very happy with your work. As far as payment is concerned you will see that you will not lack anything. The girls will grow, and you will be able to save something, and your heart will finally be satisfied. Is this true? Be brave and don’t be discouraged. Be happy in all your necessities, ask you poor Mother for advice, she will always help you.”269

The Mother of course sees that larger dimension concerning her Daughters. In reality, the Lord granted her the joy of fulfilling her wishes and she discovered in the Daughters the wonderful characteristics of grace that made them the authentic Daughters of St. Anne. And this was a great joy for her Mother’s heart.

“What a great consolation your work is for me! Well done! I clearly see that the Holy Mother has given true spirit to you and everything is growing in you. So be brave! I will always pray so that you may reach holiness and be a real champion of the Institute.”270

Motherhood a gift for the “mission”

The mystical experience of the union of fire with God, the essence of love is total and a dynamic energy for Rosa Gattorno. It mobilizes all the resources of the heart, the mind, and the body, towards the aspiration to participate in the irresistible flame of love, which came from the depth of her being:

“I feel (something), in me that I have never felt before, that makes me burn and completely consumes me. It makes me understand, it fills my mind with great and wonderful thoughts, I feel that I am and I have everything in my Love… My Good Lord, I will never stop speaking and writing about you, and if I had to, I would run into the streets and shout to everyone that they may stop offending you and they may experience only your love.”271

She finally feels involved in the love of her Good Lord who transforms everything that is in her into vital force and action. Nothing can stop her, no obstacle inside or outside her can slow down her race; the vital force comes out from her belonging totally to Him, it is all a gift as an answer, it is concentrated in the only principle; she will go everywhere shouting to everyone with a voice that is no longer her own voice. The vital flow that she conveys is that of her Good Lord. She acts in Him, for Him and with Him. Her voice is the voice of God, it is the word that penetrates hearts and converts them and turns hearts towards God. M. Rosa does wish to have any other reward or rest except to have what she loves. By using this language, Rosa Gattorno reveals herself to be a perfect woman and mother. She tends, with her own reality to take her life to other lives, until it is consumed, and in addition to this she gives her wholeness making her loving capacity grow. After having exhausted all of her own energies, she is aware that she has not given everything. The more she experiences the joy of life at the source, “nothing that belongs to this valley of tears can satisfy me” the more she feels sent to shout to everyone the Good News that God is the only Good Lord. She questions herself, she asks God about what she should do.

“How can I do, to allow others to know you; how can I convert so many souls who don’t believe today? If it was necessary, I would live a thousand lives and slowly consume these lives.” 272

God had already given an answer to her, by calling her to do His Work, by inviting her everyday into His field of Work. He helped her to become the Mother of many Daughters and her water taken from the Source, flowed from the depth of her soul into others, and like an effective, beneficial network of canals irrigates the soil of the hearts of men and women, so that life may flourish in them. Her Daughters united with her in a bond of unique love are like an extension of M. Rosa:

“Your poor Mother loves you so much, that only the dear Lord Jesus could allow you to understand the measure of this love. Oh! It is sufficient to say that I want you to be saint, and it is necessary for you to nourish your souls and to be very close to the Lord Jesus; love is intelligent, it only tries to please the beloved and to our Beloved nothing else pleases than to be loved; so we must try every method, every means to make the whole world to love and serve Him. My Daughter the moral is this: as I wish that you should become a saint, one day you may succeed in sanctifying the whole world.” 273

To make room for the Holy Spirit, to open oneself to the infinite vitality, to discover the meaning of life, to become students of love, seeking and inventing what pleases the Beloved, one must seek every means, with a new and always active creativity, every method and every means must be used to make the whole world to love and serve Him. It is important to know how to create love within us, how to make new kinds of relationships and how to create new methods of announcing, offering the total experience of being in communion and in harmony with love. M. Rosa advised Sr. Irene Carmeli, one of the nuns who taught in the school of the Parrocchietta area in Rome:

“My Daughter, do not be timid, but be completely brave concerning the Congregation of Mary (the Daughter of Mary); give encouragement to its members and you must do the same for the schools. Let others see you docile and good; The Spirit of the Institute must rule your thoughts; is this true my Daughter? Therefore, be brave, be strong and love God. Always think about Jesus, make sure that you do everything in God’s presence and make sure that you are humble, and think that the good works you do is done by our dear Teacher Jesus. Jesus by His infinite goodness deigns to humble Himself to do for us what we are unable to do because we are such meanless creatures.” 274

To always be in the presence of God, to be always more humble, to make room for our Dear Teacher Jesus… who deigns…who gives to us his continual renewal of a deep and intimate contact with the essence of life in the gift of continual motherhood. It is necessary to know how to be a manifestation and a sign of this inexhaustible motherhood and to know how to become involved.

“Love much the dear Jesus and then be cheerful so that you may inspire everyone to follow you in the apostolate of the conversion of souls.” 275

“I advice you to edify, by doing this you will attract all the young women who live in this area, be brave, because for Jesus everything that we do is little.” 276

To edify, to attract all the young women with the significant witness of the primary importance of the Love of God, with the strength and courage that develop from the life that is dedicated entirely to Him. It is important to extend God’s Kingdom of love, without pause and never going back;

“We must not loose courage, instead we must be brave, and we must fight and be victorious. Let us go ahead; we must win for the love of Jesus.”277

This militant style does not contradict her motherhood. It is a development and a fulfilment in exuberance and a fullness of life that tends to overcome everything that is evil and hostile, that is opposed to the love of Jesus. Opposed to Him who is LIFE.

4.6.1. For the “propagation of faith”

- To help others to know, love and serve God everywhere

“I will run everywhere” is her inspiration. Therefore she sends her daughters the heart to love, to shout to everyone without discrimination of race and of religion, the news of the love and the goodness of God, of His mercy and to be a gift of mercy. Her words are a force that inspires others to act.

“Be brave, it is time to work and to do important missionary work, to gain souls for God! Too many souls fall into the abyss of hell! Be brave! Blood for blood. Jesus on the Cross is completely tortured, so we are. Is this true?”278

To reach everyone is an inevitable mission that has been confirmed by the Holy Church, through the words of the Holy Father Pius IX.

“The Daughter of St. Anne must be an apostle who preaches the faith with her good actions and with example to those who are Christians, to encourage them even more and she tries to convert those who are not Christians, she possibly helps them to become Christians.” 279

She prepares the nuns and encourages them to study and to gain recognized educational qualifications, because in the school besides teaching and educating, they should teach others to love the true God, the Church and Christ’s Vicar.

“What a consolation this is! She writes to Fr. Agostino Donadio, we have accepted so many girls in our community, what a great mercy God has for this foundation. We are already starting to welcome them into our home, taking them away from sin.”280

She wishes her Daughters to be alert and to be full of zeal in the teaching of Christian doctrine. They are called to be as loving Mothers of the young, to feed their bodies, to make them grow healthy, and their spirit to make the true and good Catholics. She writes to the Superior and recommends:

“ Give my regards to Innocenza and tell her that I always hold her close to the Crucifix, so that she may give to these children the milk of the holy Religion and she may help them to be true and good Catholics.” 281

To bring souls to God: is the mother’s ever-growing wish.

“I was so pleased to hear that the Rosary is prayed in the hospital. My God what a great consolation I felt you can’t even imagine it.”282

Always and everywhere, the Daughter of St. Anne must remember this basic principle and she must remember the purpose of her vocation:

“To be holy and to be an instrument of holiness for her neighbours,”283

with her work, with her involvement in the service of charity and with her good example.

“Remember that the world is observing you and that Jesus wishes you may reflect His holiness. The example that a nun must show with her virtue and wisdom is never too much.” 284

In the missions

The intense participation in the Paschal mystery of Christ for Rosa Gattorno was not a grace that is reserved for her alone, it is a gift that is not to be used in intimacy of a life that is sheltered and hidden only in the domestic walls of a Covent; it is God’s answer to the Church, which he enriches with a New Work in dispensing salvation. Rosa is convinced of this. She frequently affirms and demonstrates it with her desire and with the solicitude of seeing the Rules being approved and the Institute being recognized by the Church. She feels that she must run everywhere and shout to everyone. In the meaning of each of these terms are the universal dimensions of the Church sent to all peoples. The Holy Father Pius IX had confirmed her missionary vocation of the Institute:

“The Daughters of St. Anne will be as many apostles who will expand throughout the world” 285

It was precisely during moments of obstacles, doubt and worry for the future of the Institute, when she saw a distant and inexplicably slow procedure for the approval of the Rules that the awareness of this vocation was clarified and strengthened in her:

“If prayer do not miraculously obtain what we seek, this vision seems rather hard to me, but the right hand of our Eternal Father in one minute can destroy all obstacles and the Daughters of St. Anne Mother of the Immaculate, will enjoy the most beautiful light in all of Catholicism and they will allow this light to shine in all nations and in these nations they will raise the standard of St. Anne.” 286

Father Tornatore with time will see this Great Work flourish throughout the catholic world.”287

This historical call for the missions will come later towards the end of 1876, through the Franciscan Father Vincenzo Rocchi and it became a reality with the departure of the first missionaries for Bolivia. She herself tells this event as a wonderful chronicle, when she writes to Sr. Gugliemina Merli:

“Oh! If you had seen yesterday the wonderful expedition of 16 Sisters, all experienced in their Vocation and so filled with a spirit of sacrifice that edified everyone! The Bishop came twice to say goodbye to them and so did all their relatives. How bravely they replied! The Holy Father sent his blessings to them. Finally they made feel envious. The Superior is Sr. Giuseppa, the one who was sent as Delegate and who lived in Pistoia; she has twelve years of Vocation, and so do the others. What a wonderful spirit! Let us bless God for it!”288

With those brave Daughters she made an agreement. Before they left, had offered them to the Sacred Heart; through Mother Rosa their hearts and their will was being offered every day, acting as a guarantor of their loyalty. They had gone to a distant Country and had left their Poor Mother, not to be separated; on the contrary to be always more united in their minds and hearts.

She sent the following message to Sr. Giuseppa Troni on January 22, 1879:

By now you will have reached your destination, all filled with good will to edify these poor people and you will also edify the entire City of La Paz, who is watching you and your actions with a thousand eyes. I live secure and peaceful about a positive outcome, because you have solemnly promised this to Jesus.”289

She had previously written while they were still travelling to give them the joy of finding her letter on the arrival:

“My Daughter I am writing a brief message to tell you that I have always received you letters during the journey, the most recent is from Spain where you tell me that you have suffered a little but you were well and now you are cheerful and happy and your courage is very great. Oh yes, this is all the work of God because the dear Jesus has communicated to you His gifts of strength and courage in the sufferings of such a long journey. I often pray and every morning I offer your sixteen hearts to the Lord, together with your will, so that God the Father may use them as he pleases and give to you strength, courage, living faith to work only for Him and never for earthly interests, tell the dear Sisters about this,

Oh! How sweet it is to suffer for Jesus! How many times have I tried to be with you but I am not worthy, my sins stop me from running quickly to the summit of dear Mount Tabor, and I have to walk on the slopes of Golgotha for the day of my departure to climb Calvary…Oh, sweet Love, strengthen my dear creatures and take all of them, all sixteen of them into your kingdom, always for all Eternity… I anxiously wait for your letters, I assure you that I count the days, the hours and I have written this message so that you may receive my news before I have to reply to your letters, that you will send to me from La Paz. Be brave! I am always with you; in the Novena of the Child Jesus, I will try to hold Him close to your hearts, as I am sure that you will do the same for me. Goodbye, may the Lord bless you, and always believe that I am your affectionate Mother.”290

She began a correspondence with those Daughters, using the postal means of communication that were available during that era:

“I am writing to you, so that I may send my letters with the British steamships that depart on the 17th, and on the 21st of each month.”291

These are the Letters of the Mother who anxiously waits for the news and who wishes to follow their everyday progress, the progress of her distant Daughters in the Nation that is unknown to her and new for them. As she knew they were filled with goodwill, with strength and with courage, given to them by Jesus, they were willing to sacrifice themselves and to suffer for Him, strong and loyal to the holy vocation that provides security and peace. But when the letters that she punctually sent did not arrive with equal punctuality, and therefore they were not replied, she felt all the burden of distance and the emptiness of the void.

“What a great sorrow it is to experience your very long silence. My God, what has happened, is she perhaps ill? For goodness sake, make sure that you write to me regularly. Have you understood? How are the Sisters? Have they settled well? Listen, I would like you not to behave as someone does, as they are out of sight, out of mind. No, I don’t wish to believe it because my Giuseppa can’t diminish the love that she nourishes in her heart for her poor Mother. Yes, is it true, it can’t be otherwise? Oh! I wish that the years would pass like a bird’s flight, so that I would have the consolation of seeing you.”292

With the passing time, the lack of news is the greatest sorrow. In the doubt that the Daughters are also deprived of her word, she seeks more secure pathways. So, on July 3, 1879, she writes:

Now I am sending the letter to the Consular, so that he may send it and to receive your news, as I feel so sad… I am incredibly upset even though my God gives me strength, my humanity experiences every kind of sorrow.”

The anguished questions overcome the persuasive reasons that oppose the maternal feelings.

“…Are they ill? Are they lacking what they need for living? How is their observance of the Rules? Finally she confesses: “I burden myself with worries, you should take them away with your letters. Oh! I would like that the days would pass, so that I may receive your news.”293

Her heart was with the Daughter and so was her thought, “From morning to evening, I always think about you.” So she had promised to them. For her it was a daily sorrow not to be able to visit them, to advice them, to help them, to personally be aware of their situation. But she trusted her Daughters, and overcame the difficulty of communications and of distance, by demanding to be clearly kept informed:

“Listen, when you write to me explain yourself a little more accurately, because your letters are so concise that I understand little, or nothing, therefore, I advice you to write more frequently and in more details. I feel sad when I see a month passing by without receiving news.”294

“Write to me often” was her repeated request. On her part, she did not neglect to provide to the Daughters her own news and news about the family:

“After you departure, I can say that I have had not a moment’s rest… I am now visiting the hospital in Capua, then I will go to Naples and then I will go to visit the Communities we have in Abruzzi Region. I stop to talk about the petty news that may provide pleasure for you. Soon I will send to you the interesting Circular that you will find to be very pleasant with so many positive news.” 295 “Here we continue to experience a demand for houses and hospitals and we always have new Postulants and Professed nuns. In a few days we will have another Profession. This year I am not inviting the Superiors because I have not succeeded in recovering from last’s year expenses. I still have some debts to pay.” 296

The best news of the Family

“The definitively approval of our Institute with the decree of the Holy Father Leo XIII.” 297

This expected and implored recognition by the Church is the fulfilment, the seal of God on His Work.

“Therefore, we are now like all Religious Organizations and no one will be able to say anything to criticize us, they may only say that we are true Daughters of the Church, the Apostolic and Roman Church.”298

One should respond with praise, loyalty and joy

“Now that the Church has approved of us, we are under a strict obligation to observe our Rules exactly; therefore, without human respect, but with frankness, we say: We can’t. Be brave, my Daughter, because without war one does not gain medals and positions, the military aim to gain positions of earthly honour and better, other positions are waiting for us; those in heaven. Oh yes! Those who go to heaven with many medals for having fought and won will certainly be given a crown and a very good position that has nothing to do with earthly sufferings. Be as strong as a lion and don’t expect too much.”299

The Mother sees in this event a sign of the blessing of the Father. Her being is expanded in the space of God in the generation of the new Daughters. She writes to Sr. Giuseppa:

“I wish that God would send to me one hundred Postulants so that I may have a great number of Daughter of St Anne, and the Holy Mother should be loved and honoured even in Bolivia, by a great number of Daughters. (The Holy Congregation of Bishops and Regulars had allowed the building of the Novitiate in La Paz. One of the Rules stipulated that six months after their Religious Profession, the Novices would complete their formation in Italy).300

“What a wonderful thing it would be if you could place together Postulants and Professed Sisters and after they have experienced their Novitiate, you would take them to me. I pray that God will answer my prayers, they are rather poor.”301

“I pray”; with prayer she opens the treasure of the Lord.”302 She prays without tiring:

Oh! Daughters, I am certain that those who live in Italy don’t inspire me to pray for them as much as you do. Oh no! I can really say this. I pray to my Crucified Lord, that He may always keep you close to Him.”303

She prays with an attitude of essential poverty and trust and with the boldness of a Mother and a new life emerges from her open dialogue with God and new gestures allow life to grow, to be developed, and to be celebrated. Others followed the first group of sixteen nuns in 1878 in 1880 and in 1882. But besides sending other nuns from Italy, the Mother opens her arms to the young autonomous vocations. She was quickly asked for and obtained from the Holy Congregation of Bishops and regulars, the authorization to open the Novitiate in La Paz, and she looks forward to the entrance of the first nuns.

“I feel that you already have a new nun and I wish that you will have many, so that you may send them to me or take them to me. Oh! I wish that time would really come!”304

She organizes the house of the religious province in 1882 entrusting it to the first Provincial Superior, Sr. Camilla Valentini. During a period of a few years, the communities developed expanding even at a notable distance from one another, strengthened by new Italian Sisters and the American Sisters. In 1884, the Daughters of St. Anne are in Brazil, two years later they are in Africa, (Assab). All of this requires a great deal of work. The Mother is directly involved. She understands the specific call, the call that she describes as the “Second vocation of the Daughters of St. Anne”. She prepares the Sisters, she sends them and when they are distant, she develops their loyalty, their courage, the gift with the Letters that are written by her. She continues to be pleased with them and to feel that she is with them.

“Well done! Keep going…Work with Jesus, do everything for Him.” 305

“Always continue to work in these arid Countries; work so that one day you will be given a beautiful crown. Be brave!”306

“Here then are other Christian souls, how fortunate you are in such beautiful missions!”307

“Are you happy in Potosi! Oh well done, dear Daughter, I embrace you in my Crucified Lord! Yes, a crown is given only to those who persevere, not to those who begin to cultivate the soil, then leave the plough and go away.”308

“Oh! You are so blessed for the sake of Jesus309

“You have crossed the sea and travelled a long way to become even more holy, ready to experience martyrdom.”

The secret of the development of the Family of St. Anne in the territories of the missions is therefore to be found in the long imploring of the Mother with open arms in an offering of oneself, and in intimate communion with her Crucified Bridegroom in a complete gift: “A life for a life and blood for blood.” It is in the participation of the Daughters of St. Anne in the generative charismatic force because they as the Daughters of St. Anne also produce fruits: “If you will do well and will produce good fruits, everyone will want to have a branch of your tree.”310

4.6.2. In the service of charity

After the death of her husband, Rosa Gattorno clearly experiences a new vocation towards the service of “charity”. In 1858 was her a year of mourning, of upheaval and of… grace. It was a birth of a new way of being and of loving. We have already observed this when we mentioned in the introduction to the memoirs. The scope of the narrative is significant, even before she expresses her feelings, the feelings that she experienced at the beginning of the wonderful adventure with God, she note:

“I dedicated myself with greater fervour to works of charity, visiting hospitals, the poor, the sick in their homes, helping them financially when I could and serving them in all their needs.”

The pedagogy of God developed from the reality of life, from daily events, from reality and develops in the constant line of dialogue and of the gift of salvation. The relationship of new love has a transforming power: “It shifts the attention from self to others” And these others become the brother/sisters-children-of God, loved by God to whom he Himself sends us. Charity has its fundamental law that is the point of view and the measure of God: “Love others as I have loved you.” Mother Rosa understands the pedagogy of God and played according to the rules of the game. She allowed herself to love. She felt purified by the Blood of Christ and she opened herself to the Father’s mercy. He, her dear “All” put his sensitivity, His impulses and the ability to suffer to relieve the brothers and sister into her heart.

“Nothing seems as sweet on this earth, nothing! I can only feel one thing: Charity! Oh! What great joy one experiences when one can do well and help to return to God the one who is out of the way! Yes, the soul rejoices in charity and it feels great pleasure in seeing the well being of creatures even if the sacrifice costs much sorrow, it is always a consolation to see the soul relieved.” 311

From the deep openness of heart to poverty and indigence, compassion is liberated, the delicate welcoming of the Mother for her weak creature is manifested and the joyful delight of life is experienced. From the death of self, flows a new ability to love: the acceptance of the wounded “invalids.”

This deep feeling of mercy is a gift from the dear Eternal Father. She receives it by contemplating the Son who has burdened Himself with all the sufferings of the human race to heal all people and to make them happy he has become Bread, the Food of salvation in the Eucharist. In Him she may accept all the consequences of accepting evil and the sorrow of others. God did not ask her for the impossible, for a life of absurd suffering. He gave her the joy of associating her to His redemptive work: she participated in joy the explosive happiness of life the fruit of mercy: the return to the Father of those who are on the wrong track; the healing of the body and of the spirit, the well-being, the good health of those who are ill. He made Mother Rosa an agent of His charity. She offers herself to the service of love.

“Use this miserable instrument as your servant”

and she feel accepted and involved:

“I will give everything to you, everything that you ask me to give for the sake of the good of the souls that are close to you and for the sake of those whom you care for.” 312

She understands that her charity must be inventive, she must reach the depth of suffering, and she must enter into unity of being with those who suffer. Her Lord the Crucified Good Lord did the same:

“He allowed me to see how and in which ways I achieved results in my work of charity, what I received from Him for the little work that I did and how pleased He was to see me so keen to obtain this treasure. Oh! the joy that I felt! I was never satisfied with my work… My God, how great is this treasure! In your immensity, you my Good Lord practised charity by pouring your Blood and by dying on the Cross for our salvation. Oh! Charity.”313

The joy, the deep, intimate joy, fulfilling through the mystical experiences is the fulfilment of the Saviour promises: “Blessed are the merciful, because they will find mercy.” God is love and those who lives in love lives in God and God lives in them. Live in the present. He is the one who liberates tender compassion in Mother Rosa’s heart. He lives in her and she lives in Him. These promises are fulfilled in the mystical experience; through this experience Rosa loves in faith. God approaches her, sends her to the brothers/sisters, whom he loves in her heart of flesh. The brothers/sisters bring her to God by communicating his love to her. Therefore, she exults with unspeakable joy. Even the plan of her humble daily life, she sees every person being close to God and the poor, the invalids irresistibly attract her heart.

The Son of God became one of them. From the ecstasy, that involves her in the fire of charity; she went to hospitals, she talks about this in her memoirs where she finds all her happiness. Nothing discourages her: the healing of the wounds was her favourite activity, because she felt that she was healing the wounds of her Lord Jesus and she became so involved with this work that she had to think about other topics not remain enraptured in Him.314 Therefore the cry of the poor echoes in her profoundly:

“Oh! The poor who cry… what a terrible winter! I assure you that it makes me sigh!” 315

Mercy reaches the deepest parts of her mind in the desire to become as a miracle of love: bread for the poor:

“I would like to attract everyone’s attention to offer help to those in need…If I could make gold come out of my veins, do you know what I would do? … I would take it out of my veins until it would become dry.”316

4.6.3. Her pedagogy of charity

In this dynamism of “charity”, enters the teaching of Mother Rosa, about “doing” and “how to do” works of charity. When Daughters of St. Anne become receptacles of charity, and allow God’s charity in themselves, they are born again in the novelty of the Spirit; they are able to develop and to produce positive results; charity then becomes a fountain in them; it is an extension of the gift of motherhood:

“I hope that soon I will see my Daughters forgetting their own selves and completely united with Jesus, with charity, patience, confidence In God, courage and faith.”

Involved, penetrated by the energy of the “fire” of charity and dedicated to Him.

This is her desire:

“Oh; Love and don’t be afraid of the one you love, only be afraid of disappointing Him.”317

It is important for the Daughters to allow themselves to be loved by Jesus, and to love Him passionately.”

“Love, love Jesus, become victims of charity”318.

She advised the Daughters to develop the same feelings that she felt, the same feelings of “compassion”, the same anxiety, the same mercy, like Mary and like her mother Saint Anne. She advised them to be mothers with their actions, by being servants and being a gift of life.

This mission must be accomplished in the dynamism of fire of the Holy Spirit, as strong, joyful and solid women; not by becoming lost in trivial, in vague words and “ideas”, things this that deceive the mind, and are only useful for disturbing us, and for making us angry; on the contrary we “should remain positive always reasoning with the Crucifix in front of us “319

The Daughters should be ready to lose their own life “with unlimited charity and without reward, with a silent and hidden sacrifice”320

Mother Rosa teaches with her life. She communicates the evangelical values that she lives, and above all “charity, the queen of all virtues”, and in expressing to the Daughters her intimate life, she becomes a teacher of charity, she outlines the ideal Daughter of St. Anne.

She writes to Sr. A Adelaide Pezzoni, on 4.2.1871, who was then the superior of the motherhouse community in Piacenza:

“Oh! My Eternal Father! Daughter, the heart of this God is so wonderful and loving that there are no words to express it; Daughter do you know what is important in this great and immense heart? Charity and she is the queen. Therefore, those who don’t have charity, can’t say that they are sharing in this great love; what a great pleasure we feel when we relive the need of the poor, it is as awakening in us of a completely pure love towards these creatures, even if they might be repellent, we must be ready even give our blood to assist the poor or the indigent.”

“To be apart”, to be sharing in the Father’s charity means that he takes us out of our petty programs, our petty measure and communicates to us his very strong love, a new way of being, of living and of operating. He loves us, and He loves through us when we assist the poor. God expects us to take care of the poor, the weak, the children, the creatures who appear rather insignificant in as far as the world is concerned. It is necessary for us to serve the least of our brothers and sisters, loving them in His heart, recognising His mysterious and simple presence in them. It is a blessing to participate in His creative and saving power; it is a revelation made to “children”, to those whom He shows His charity and His Father’s face. It is a free communication in his very pure love of unlimited mercy.

Here are the sources of the mission of the Daughters of St Anne. Mother Rosa lives the Father’s mercy without any reservation and acts as mediator for her Daughters.

She wrote to one of the Daughters, Sr. Carlotta Biagini, on February 13, 1874:

“Daughter, learn to love the Dear God, and to give your love only to him; everything to Him, live for Him and love only Him. Oh love of our Good Lord, when will I see my Daughter inflamed by your love? She is dedicated in her life; she is ready to give all her blood to You, therefore give to her strength and the love of dedication.”

As a real Mother she guarantees to God her Daughter’s loyalty certain about the reply of love: she is dedicating her life she is ready to give all her blood.

United in Christ

In her brave language, Mother Rosa communicates objectively, without using explicit personal references, her own mystical experience, by using symbolic language.

She speaks of “fire”, of “enjoyment”, of “a robe stained with the blood of Christ”, of “the way of the Cross”, of the “Good Lord.” Leaving aside the deepening of her mystical itinerary, that is irrelevant to our subject, we soon notice one of the symbols: the blood which is closely connected with the symbol per excellence: the Crucifix. This symbolic word highlights the mystical experience of Rosa Gattorno, of the immense merciful love of the Father in Christ Jesus. In the Passion of Christ, in the blood that he shed on the Cross, Mother Rosa understands the unlimited love of the Father, His mercy towards her, a poor sinner and towards all people; a love of tenderness, of mercy, of compassion, of forgiveness. One passion that of Christ, lived in the Incarnation, taken to the extremes of surrendering of Himself to the shedding of his Blood on the Cross up to the last drop. This is an open book.

In the pierced heart of Jesus, she is overwhelmed by the fire of the Spirit of love. She is overwhelmed so that she may become a gift of maternal tenderness to each Daughter and to her neighbours in the service of charity.

She participates in the mystery of her dear Crucified Lord sharing in his passion and she leads her Daughters towards Him, so that they may experience love in a living dimension.

She wrote to Sr. Vincenza Rapallino, on 20.10.1871:

“Today, Friday, I took my Daughter with me to the wonderful wounded side of Jesus, so that He may convert her, making her united with Him, not living to experience fleshly-carnal feelings, but only to become an instrument of holiness to our souls.

My Daughter, accept your poor Mother’s advice, escape frequently in to the loving shelter of our Jesus, and enter in it, especially when you feel sad and you experience some problems.

That is the precious moment when we are certain to find every kind of consolation: everything is forgotten and remain only the joys of it; we only experience the desire to endure suffering because the more we are burdened with sorrows, the more Jesus opens His very loving wounded side to us…Let us take our cross and say to the Eternal Father, please look at me and may your glance strengthen me, so that I may not only carry this dear cross on my shoulders, but that I may also bravely hold it close to my chest.”

Being with Jesus, hiding in his very loving wounded side is therefore, for Rosa Gattorno, the result of Trinitarian communion, in the mystical participation of the saving suffering of Jesus. These “extraordinary” gifts are given by the Father to anyone and in any way that He wishes and they are certainly not the measure of holiness, that accompany her.

However, all her Daughters are called to imitate her in the gift “without measure”, to the Father in Christ, and to work tirelessly, in the works of charity to their neighbours. They are called to carry the cross “close to their chest” being the cross life. “Without the Cross we can do nothing good”.

To carry the cross for the Daughters of St. Anne means to love Christ, to live in Christ, to accept as He did: “Every kind of suffering”, to work for Him, without ever considering one’s own interests, to see Him in every little one, in the lonely, poor, and destitute person.

“We see in these dear invalids the person of our Lord, the dear Saviour! This is really a wonderful thought: that we are healing Jesus!”

Blessed are you who can always see Him with your eyes and in your heart…Jesus in the hospitalized patients!”

“Let Jesus be in all your works! Oh! Infinite sweetness, without Him nothing is good neither beautiful. With Him, we have everything, we don’t lack anything, we can be certain that we have Him with us, and we are sure of running along the right path, and that we are doing everything that He wishes us to do. Let us obey and we will be certain, certain to please Him and to be with Him for eternity”.321

The houses of the sick, the hospitals, every place where the works of “charity” is carried on, is Calvary for the Daughters of St. Anne,322 the space of the salvation of people, in the gift of one self through daily sacrifice expressed in a thousand forms, in the great and the small actions. All of these actions are inspired and marked by the maternal tenderness that is poured in their hearts and by the joy of the Spirit.

The Spirit moves the Daughters of St. Anna.

To live in Jesus, to see Him in one’s neighbours and to spend one’s life to become “victims of charity” is a gift of the Spirit.

The Spirit, the Governor, as Mother Rosa calls Him, inspires in his loyal Daughters “heavenly insights”: light, heat, warmth, strength like that of intoxicating liquor, grant them different qualities of being and of operating.

The Spirit removes everything that is obscure, a burden, closed, hidden, and sad. The Mother sees this different type of life, she experiences the transformation in faith, in hope, in charity, in patience, in courage, in the life of her Daughters, their affective participation in the sorrows of others, their zeal for the good of their brothers and their acceptance in a new way, of the sorrows of others, their inner peace and their happiness and joy.

She wishes that her Daughters might have an abundance of these gifts.

About joy, as an expression and a outcome of charity, she insists.

“Love Jesus and you will be happy”.323

The Spirit of love pours in to the hearts of her beloved Daughters: happiness, comfort, sweet honey, strength, very sweet nectar, pleasures, delights, caresses, goodness, food, drink, relief, rest.324

This image-symbolic language takes us to the heart of Mother Rosa’s mystical experience. She is given the grace of experiencing the wealth of life in love, the fruits of charity that, as a pure gift of the Spirit, are being produced in the Family of the Daughters of St. Anne. She proclaims this with joy, in a letter to Sr. A. Celsa Speranza:325

“Heaven rejoices for the good works done by the Daughters of St. Anne, the good work that is done in the vineyard of the Lord, and the Angels themselves walk about, picking the mature fruits, and they take them to the throne of God the Father. And the sweet Jesus with a glance that is full of satisfaction admires the fruits of His very precious Blood.

He, the loving Lord, infinite in His love, has bought so much wealth for us, that he could use to raise our poor souls to the summits of Eternal life, that are only gained by hard work and by enduring suffering. Love …love!”

With the family style: compassionate love, faith, and hope.

In the instructions regarding the practise of charity, the Mother, besides her personal experience refers to the Rules of 1869, interpreting them with creative vision and with lively freedom. The Rule in Chapter 8, Paragraph 1, says:

“My Daughters, my heart was a sea of compassion for the spiritual and physical sufferings of my neighbours. In this, I was a perfect reflection of Jesus Christ; whose dearest work, the work he most advised His followers to do was assisting the sick.

To make us willing to do this service of charity, that is most repugnant to our perverse nature, He assures us that the help that we give to the sick is equivalent to helping Him.

You, my Daughters are called to imitate me in this compassionate charity.”

Mother Rosa observes:

“It is necessary that all the Daughters should remember Jesus, the Divine Model, to correct their wrong way of thinking and of operating especially regarding the charity that I recommend so much, and for which our Mother St. Anne, worked so much.”326

“You who work hard for Jesus will be consoled, because in helping the sick with charity (and this is the kind of charity that our dear Mother St. Anne had) in helping those sick, you help Jesus who is in them. Ah! What a wonderful thought, my Daughters!”327

“You should know that when you are in the presence of the sick you are in the presence of Jesus, you will behave with humility and modesty, you will speak about topics that will help them and you will edify the witness”.328

Mother Rosa said:

“ I recommend you the assistance to the sick, to go to them with love and with respect, as if you would go to visit Jesus; if happens to fall asleep, make sure that wake up again and will do everything possible to remain awake; (The nursing nuns also worked at night shifts).

I must think that I am in the presence of Jesus and that He will considers everything that I do for the sick.

You see, I went to help the invalids for 25 years, and I felt as if I was going to Heaven. You see this is the only consolation that we can have on this earth; I haven’t experienced it again after I ceased to do this type of work.

Yes, you should do everything in a spirit of faith. I am in this hospital, am healing this lady whose body is filled with worms, I am relieving her suffering. Ah! What a delight feeling, when I think about relieving a person who belongs to Jesus; there is no other type of work that offers so much consolation: to return to my house in the morning and to say: I have healed the wound of my Jesus! You would say to me: but I haven’t experienced these delights; ah! This means that you did not do this work with a spirit of faith! Why do we let so much hard work be done in vain? Why do we act as if we are so many servants? Ah! yes the Lord has always shown favouritism to the nurses!”329

“My Daughter, among the works of my Institute, the function of helping the sick is the noblest and the most meritorious. With this work you my Daughter imitate that compassionate charity of my heart towards the sufferings of people; this work made me very similar to my Immaculate Daughter and to my Nephew Jesus…Here then my Daughter, this is the gain that you must remember when you think about your help to the sick, what you gain is that you, as my Daughter, carry with you my compassionate charity towards your brothers/sisters, that charity that will light a flame in your heart, that will make you inflamed by a desire to make God happy, and to glorify Him in eternal health, the health of the mind and bodies of your brothers/sisters , and therefore you will feel a great sorrow, of sadness and pain, to see them as distant and in danger of losing their eternal spiritual health, a sorrow and an anguish that will eventually make you die sad and crucified with Christ Jesus”.330

From these principles Mother Rosa develops norms for practical behaviour during her conferences with the nurses:

“For goodness sake, don’t abandon the invalids who are ill to attend Mass; if you do this, how can you receive communion, after having abandoned the invalid Jesus, who needed your help? What will you say to Him? What will He say to you?

You have abandoned me while suffering and now you come to receive me? If this happens on a feast day inform the superior, who will send two other nuns and will to inform me. Mass is celebrated also later during the day, and then you will be able to say to Jesus: Jesus, I have suffered for you throughout the night, I have taken a soul to you, and now I have come too receive my reward, to receive you in my soul”.

And she continues:

“There are men who don’t wish to know anything about religion. Don’t talk about it to them; many times it is better to leave them alone. Let them be amused and you will see that eventually they will return to religion and they will do what you ask them to do”.331

The Daughters of St. Anne will always try to see how much light there is in the hearts of men, because they know that God is the merciful Father, who always waits for His children to come back to Him. By serving the corporal needs of the invalids, they will practise the service of light for the souls, so that the flame of faith may shine and the brothers may enjoy salvation.

”My Daughter you must know how to unite together the assistance of the invalids with exercises of piety that are set out in the Holy Rules. From these holy exercises you may receive that enlightened faith that will help you understand that you are serving Jesus by helping the invalids, that strong hope that through the exhaustion of your strength and of your body, will allow you to feel that delightful and eternal life that will be given to you as a reward for the loss of the present life, that charity that by serving the invalids only seeks that complacency that your God feels in having you as a companion in relieving the body of the invalid, in his illnesses, but with that intention, that same intention that God uses to relieve suffering, that is the intention to heal his soul from the illness of sin, if he experiences that type of illness and to unite him with God”.332

In order that the Daughters would not distance themselves from that sublime mission Mother Rosa prays without pausing:

“I will always offer your hearts and your will to the Lord my Daughters, so that God may use them as He pleases and He may give you strength, courage and a strong faith to work only according to His will and never, never for earthly interest”.333

Hope gives wing to the desire and to the meaning of life:

“My beloved Daughters of St. Anna be brave, because one day you will see your God, and you will enjoy your reward for the hard work you have done and those who have worked harder, will be rewarded even more”.334

The maternal style in service.

The Rule of 1869 definitely marks with emphasis the fundamental attitude of the Daughters of St. Anne in their work of charity.

“You must think of yourself as a mother”.

It is a compendium; one may say that it is a symphony of the feelings and of the personal spiritual richness proper of a person in her being WOMAN. It means gratuity, attentiveness, humility, meekness, patience; to be mother for the Daughter of St Anne means compassion (suffering with others), effective service that overcomes evil and seeks the good.

Mother Rosa told the Daughters:

“You are the Mothers of the poor sick, you will love them with a maternal love, you will pray for them, and you will weep for their physical and spiritual sufferings”.335

Mother advised the Daughters:

“Help one another and remember to imitate the charity of our Mother St. Anne that is: authentic charity towards our neighbours. Love those who suffer, suffer with them”.336

“Treat your neighbours with kindness and love”.337

“Daughter, be good to everyone and give a good example to the dear sick”.338

“Oh! I would like to see you in the great wards (of the hospitals), close to the bed of Jesus, to heal Him and to attend to His needs! And so He gives to you His feeling of love; every morning I tell Him to consume yourself in him.”339

Mother Rosa is the Mother of the Daughters that “God has entrusted to her”.340

“You will not cease to give to them every type of physical and spiritual relief…every innocent consolation, so that in this way, they will see in you a mother ready to forget herself and only think about making them happy”.341

“I keep them close to my Crucified Lord (the teachers), so that they may give to the children that are entrusted to them the milk of holy Religion, so that they grow in becoming true servants of the Lord and also good Catholics”.342

“The teachers should make an effort to attract the hearts of the young girls towards them in such a way that will make the young girls to be docile, good and dear to the Lord and they may begin to live in the Lord. How sad it is the thought of how many hearts I could have given to Jesus, and instead, how many hearts because of my fault, have become lost”.343

The maternal style used by Mother Rosa in teaching her Daughters is not a marginal aspect of her charism.

It is the central value of her charism in the sense that it expresses, through the lifestyle and by positive actions the Fathers’ merciful love, which is revealed in the evangelical ideal of clarity expressed by Jesus: love without seeking a response, give even your own life if needed without expecting a reward, lose that other may grow. This is the way the Father does in Christ. Acting in a unity of love to please the Father and in strict union with the Crucified Lord, is at the summit of the desires of Mother Rosa, it is her response:

“Ah! Dear good Lord, I have provided food, I have propagated your Word, and I have done all of these on the wings of your providence!”344

In the Family of the Holy Mother of Mary Immaculate, there cannot be any other point of view, any other style, and any other law, beside the maternal gift of the service of life. She has already actualized this new, creative, and different way of life in the Mother House, since the origins of the Institute:

“We give to them (she is speaking of the poor and abandoned girls), food, we take them away from sin, we teach them to love God. The Eternal Father will think about the rest. What do we have here my dear?”345

Who gave to us the income that we have used to help these hungry girls? God did. Yes my dear, we must be prudent, but today we must even be more prudent because for the sake of doing little works of charity, we Sisters are paid too much.

What a horror! This is a wrong attitude and our holy Institute, that is full of charity, rejects it.

Be brave and let us go forward! I accept here all the Postulants that we can find”.346

The Daughters must accept this specific quality, of being and acting, if they wish to live according to their peculiar gift of their Religious Family, that qualifies their “Following” of Christ: to reveal God’s maternal face, to be a sign and an instrument of the Fathers’ mercy, of the intimacy of a love that “touches” them, that is deep moved by the poverty of the children, by the suffering that they experience, by their cry of pain, by the sadness of their being abandoned.

A love that is close to Christ becomes strong by the power of His Cross, the Daughters participate in their interior thoughts and feelings, to the life Jesus, in His passion for human being, they are involved in a mission of productive salvation.

They perform this mission with the greatest loyalty to the foundational charism of Mother Rosa. In this loyalty is the special strength of the Family of the Daughters of St. Anne.

In the biographical and spiritual itinerary of Mother Rosa, as seen from the charismatic aspect of her maternal mission, two terminal moments are evident:

The first moment, climaxes in her human maternity (the years from 1853 to 1857, the birth of her three children).

The remote education that happened from her childhood to the end of adolescence, and the more specific pre-matrimonial and matrimonial preparation contributed to this moment.

The second moment is focused on her spiritual motherhood (from 1866, the foundation of the Institute, until her death in 1900).

It is the epilogue of an experience of extreme sorrow -the impact of the death of her husband, and the death of her youngest son- and of the profound encounter with God.

She discovers her own vocation in the Church, in the gift of herself to the participation in the mission of salvation, through the “propagation of faith”, and the service of charity to the poor and the sick.

In her relationship with God, her faith has followed an evolutionary line of development that originated while she was still married.

For her, God was fundamentally the Provident Lord, who loves His children, who cares for them, who guides them towards the good, who shows His will through the “commandments”.

She feels certain about this faith, and she conducts her life by aiming to reach the centre of the will of God, and she allows herself to be guided in this direction, also by the mediation of those who represent it.

In this nucleus of “structural” faith, she experiences the joys of motherhood.

Being inspired by the intimate experiences of life, she is enriched by them. Her feminine being is extended in being a mother. She participates in the Creator’s vital energy. Having reached this moment of climax however, the way does not follow the plan that she had outlined.

A sudden change interrupted the normal development that she had reasonably planned and expected. Her plan to develop a family, that was intelligently planned and actualized, collapsed.

At this point God entered her family history, so that it may again become the encounter of His wish to save all men.

This fact places Mother Rosa Gattorno in God’s school directly, so that she allows herself to be guided every day by God in the unpredictable events of her life.

For her, God becomes more important than any type of evidence, He is no longer just the God of obedience, He is the God of LOVE, who gives His only Son for the salvation of people.

Mother Rosa opens her soul to His power. And when, through the mediation of Pope Pius the IX, God requests the sacrifice of her children she, like Abraham, definitely joins His plan.

“I feel as strong as a giant”. Her faith in this way reaches the apex of unconditional obedience.

In the Church, she establishes a New Family, the Daughters ‘of the promise”. With the new mission, she receives a new name: MOTHER.

(In the Religious Family of the Daughters of St. Anna, the present custom is to call “Mother”, only the Superior General, in their position as representative of Mother Rosa.)

From the numerous Daughters that she formed, emerges the summit of Divine mercy, that reaches Mother Rosa through the Blessed Womb of Mary, who closely united with her Mother St Anne; the shape, character and heart of the Family is formed in the Work, that prolongs the Family of the Mother of Mary Immaculate in the plan of salvation.

For the sake of the Work of God Mother Rosa dedicates her entire life, to the extreme limit.

This is proved by the tangible facts, and these facts are so well known that they do not need to be supported by the accounts of witnesses, or by other forms of collaboration.

It is sufficient enough to mention only one that, because of the authority of the witness, Father P.G.B. Tornatore, who was very close to her as a co-founder of the Family, and for the terms in which it is expressed, seems to be a synthesis of all the other accounts provided by witnesses: “What a Lady! How she sacrifices herself for the Institute! Oh, she is a creature who is really loyal to her God. She only lives for the purpose to do the Work chosen by God for her to do”. 347

This dedication is part of her maternal being. She gives her gift of motherhood for the Church, to the poor, to girls who are in difficulties, to the sick, to all those who need her love, with an immediate response.

She is a gift of motherhood first of all to the Daughters, involving them in the new type of presence, and of service in the church.

The Daughters, who are called by her to do the Work of the Father, have discovered what the Spirit had already inspired them to do. They themselves reflected in her attitudes, they express their desires in her, they listen to her and they follow her.

From this convergence of ideals and of aspirations the Family of the Holy Mother of Mary Immaculate is established and developed with a significant growth and success.

The Mother accepts every Daughter, as a tender plant that must be cultivated; she cares for her, she strengthens her, with that very human love, maternal love, “that is a great hidden strength, a warmth that is poured on the seed”.348

It is warmth that actualizes in each Daughter, and in the whole Family, the action of the Spirit.

She is all for the well being of the Daughters, and for the strengthening of the Work, with a fighting type of energy, without pause and without measure.

“My dear, I can assure you that this miserable Mother has done everything, has said everything, her thought has always been focused on your well being, and I neglected my own needs a thousand times, for the sake of your well being”.349

Mother Rosa recognizes the spiritual richness that the Daughters use to participate in the Work of God, and she is pleased about this. In her deep humility, she feels that she is receiving so much from them. She thanks them. Only God can give a reward and she asks Him to do so:

“My blessed creatures, believe that your poor Mother will be rewarded, will be eternally grateful to you. On this earth she prays for her Daughters, for their spiritual and bodily good, so that she may leave them strong, and firm in virtue and in faith; in Heaven, if I go there by the mercy of God the Father, you can be certain that I will pray so much that, if my prayers are granted, you will certainly be happy”.350

At the end of her life on earth, on May 6, 1900, she had many Daughters to pray for, almost 4,000.

Her maternal mission has not ended with the end of great life. In the “eternal joy” the greatest aspiration in her life, she contemplates the mystery of her God: the Eternal Father, Christ her Good Lord, the Spirit of overwhelming love.

She lives in the fullness of life, she lives in today’s situation, in the way that she defined herself “your Mother for all eternity”. She is the womb of the new spiritual lives. Her numerous Daughters who follow her feel conquered by the Spirit, by her charism, by her vital energy that penetrates the reality in the dimensions of space and time, of breadth and length.

Present with God, she is also present, in a mysterious way, in the Family of the Daughters of St. Anna, in her Family, with witness of her life and very relevant teaching; a teaching that is very appropriate for the needs of today, a teaching that is contained in her written works, first of all, her correspondence, that the present research has frequently consulted. By using these sources, one may discover Mother Rosa’s intimate spiritual world. One may discover the intimacy of her world;351 one may know “the great works accomplished by her, by the power of the Good Lord, and of the Holy Mother”.

To discover her again in the vital and strong relationship of motherhood to allow oneself to be nourished by her ideas, the ideas of the Mother, means for every Daughters of St. Anne, to accept the dynamic force of the “charism”, and to live according to it’s teachings in the historical present era that is quickly going towards the Twenty First Century.

To make it a living and actual in an intelligent form of maternal dedication, that is inventive and inexhaustible, by expressing and by witnessing the Motherhood of God, that wishes to express itself in a love of merciful tenderness to every man and every woman in our distant and restless world.

It means, above all, to see God as being “close” to us, as walking with us, today, just as he did yesterday.

We must allow ourselves to be guarded by God, we must allow ourselves to be welcomed by God, and to be liberated from fear, that today is felt more than it was felt yesterday, and we must free ourselves from the alienating conditioning of “popular culture”, we must listen to Mother Rosa’s story and to our story, in the TRUTH and in the clarity and in the shining clarity of His WORD, the only Word, that gives “meaning” to life, to our origins and to our destiny.

It means to accept the Father’s plan, to walk in His path, with courage and loyalty, to look to the future, towards the shining Mountain of freedom: Calvary.

It means to be and to go, always with Him, in Him and for Him.

Mother Rosa explains this to us with her overwhelming force with her very relevant witness:

“….Go ahead, the earth is great, the field is immense. Enter, and never turn back, always think about what you haven’t done, not about what you have already done. It is wrong to believe that we have already done something”.352
